jobs.title: Construction Field Engineer, Structural
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.




THE ROLE:

The Civil/Structural Construction Field Engineer will serve as the site project team’s field-level subject matter expert for structural, concrete, building envelope, and site/civil construction supporting brownfield construction.

This position will support the rehabilitation and modernization of existing facility infrastructure as well as installation of new systems required to support advanced manufacturing operations. The Field Engineer will work closely with the internal site project team, design team, general contractor, trade contractors, geotechnical engineers, testing agencies, equipment vendors, and internal manufacturing stakeholders.

The Field Engineer will be expected to have working knowledge of industrial infrastructure to support the Superintendent in evaluating field conditions, coordinating construction activities, tracking physical progress, and driving resolution of technical and construction issues before they affect the project schedule.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

Schedule & Progress Tracking 

 - Work directly with the Superintendent to drive execution of the construction schedule.

 - Understand structural and civil milestones, equipment foundation completion dates, equipment delivery dates, and critical-path activities.

 - Participate in weekly construction planning and coordination meetings.

 - Perform weekly field walks and track measurable installed quantities.

 - Track progress for demolition, excavation, aggregate placement, reinforcing steel, concrete, structural steel, underground utilities, paving, and other applicable work.

 - Validate contractor-reported progress against actual installed work.

 - Identify activities that are trending behind schedule and determine the underlying constraints.

 - Support three- and six-week look-ahead planning.

 - Identify design, material, equipment, manpower, access, inspection, testing, safety, and quality constraints affecting upcoming work.

 - Work with the Superintendent and contractors to develop recovery plans when work falls behind schedule.

 - Coordinate foundation completion dates directly with manufacturing equipment delivery and installation requirements.



RFIs and Submittal Coordination/Tracking

 - Review structural and civil RFIs for technical completeness, constructability, field applicability, and potential schedule impacts.

 - Maintain a log of outstanding RFIs that could affect upcoming construction activities and drive timely resolution.

 - Review concrete mix designs, reinforcing steel shop drawings, structural steel shop drawings, anchor systems, crane submittals, civil materials, building envelope systems, and other technical submittals.

 - Review equipment foundation requirements provided by manufacturing equipment vendors.

 - Verify approved RFIs and submittals are incorporated into field installations and documented as a redline set to be converted to as-builts.

 - Coordinate discrepancies between design documents, existing conditions, geotechnical information, surveys, and equipment vendor requirements.

 - Identify long-lead structural or civil materials that could impact field execution.



Quality and Safety Support 

 - Verify structural and civil construction complies with approved drawings, specifications, submittals, RFIs, manufacturer requirements, and applicable codes and standards.

 - Verify required inspections, testing, checklists, preparatory meetings, and quality documentation are completed in advance of scheduled construction.

 - Participate in preparatory, initial, and follow-up inspections as appropriate.

 - Identify deficient or nonconforming work and coordinate corrective actions.

 - Coordinate with third-party testing and inspection agencies.

 - Monitor soil density and compaction testing.

 - Monitor reinforcing steel and embed inspections.

 - Monitor concrete sampling, slump, air content, temperature, cylinder testing, and strength results.

 - Verify required Activity Hazard Analyses (AHAs), excavation permits, lift plans, hot-work permits, demolition plans, fall-protection planning, confined-space documentation, and other applicable safety requirements are completed before work begins.

 - Ensure required safety documentation and approvals are addressed sufficiently in advance so they do not become schedule constraints.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Construction Management, or related field; significant equivalent industrial construction experience may be considered.

 - 3-5+ years of structural/civil construction experience with a strong preference for industrial or manufacturing facilities.

 - Demonstrated experience with concrete foundations and structural modifications.

 - Strong understanding of concrete construction, reinforcing steel, structural steel, earthwork, and civil construction means and methods.

 - Ability to read and interpret structural drawings, civil drawings, geotechnical reports, specifications, shop drawings, and equipment foundation requirements.

 - Experience reviewing RFIs, submittals, shop drawings, and technical documentation.

 - Experience tracking installed quantities and construction production.

 - Working knowledge of construction quality-control, inspection, testing, and documentation requirements.

 - Ability to independently identify field problems and drive them toward resolution.




WHAT WILL SET YOU APART

 - 8+ years of industrial or manufacturing construction experience.

 - Experience with large-scale brownfield manufacturing facility modernization.

 - Experience with heavy industrial or precision manufacturing equipment foundations.

 - Experience modifying thick reinforced concrete slabs and existing foundations within operating or existing industrial facilities.

 - Experience with GPR, concrete demolition, excavation, subgrade preparation, reinforcing steel, concrete placement, and equipment anchorage.

 - Experience with structural steel modifications within existing buildings.

 - Experience with overhead bridge cranes, crane runway structures, and crane modifications.

 - Experience with building envelope rehabilitation.

 - Experience with industrial site/civil and underground utility construction.

 - Experience coordinating geotechnical engineers and third-party testing/inspection agencies.

 - Experience supporting defense, aerospace, shipbuilding, automotive, heavy manufacturing, or similarly complex industrial facilities.


BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees

 - 401k

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need.

 - Flexible vacation policy

 - Equity

Lush North America supports over 262 (and growing!) retail stores in Canada and the USA, a mail order business based in Vancouver, and manufacturing centers in both Vancouver and Toronto.

In this role, you are curious about the diverse needs of our teams and work closely with cross-functional partners to design and deliver events that are clear in purpose and impactful in experience. You are highly organized and adaptable, able to manage multiple priorities while anticipating challenges and finding creative solutions. With a strong attention to detail and a passion for continuous improvement, you are always looking for ways to elevate the experience—bringing fresh ideas, leading fearlessly with thoughtful feedback, and a commitment to delivering meaningful moments for our people.

As a growing business, we value individuals who can evolve with us—those who are curious, proactive, and grounded in purpose. Our teams are driven by connection, experience, and impact, and this role is instrumental in shaping how we come together across the organization .Lush thrives with people that can adapt and evolve to the needs of our business. Our Lush staff live with purpose, finding their personal connection with the values of our business, bringing their work and life paths into one holistic journey. #mylushlife

• Work with HQ Teams to refine and improve events, as well as manage operating costs. Critique events and budgets, etc. to improve on for next time

• Continually seek unique and innovative methods to improve by identifying industry trends, new concepts and innovative practices to constantly evolve our meetings to the next level

Guest Experience & Service Delivery

• Anticipate guest needs and preferences to create a seamless and memorable experience
• Maintain a polished, professional presence consistent with Wynn’s luxury hospitality standards
• Build rapport with resort guests, golfers, members, and VIP patrons to encourage guest loyalty and repeat visits
• Create a welcoming atmosphere that complements both the refined dining experience and golf club setting
• Ensure every guest interaction reflects Wynn’s commitment to exceptional service

Order Taking & Menu Expertise

• Accurately take and enter food and beverage orders, including modifications, allergies, and dietary restrictions
• Provide informed recommendations based on guest preferences, occasions, and dining goals
• Clearly communicate menu descriptions, ingredients, preparations, and featured specialties

• Promote signature menu items and beverage pairings to enhance the guest experience

Food & Beverage Service

• Deliver food and beverages according to established presentation and service standards
• Perform wine, cocktail, and beverage service in accordance with luxury dining expectations
• Monitor tables continuously to ensure proper pacing of courses and overall guest satisfaction
• Coordinate service timing to accommodate individual guests, large parties, golf outings, and special events
• Ensure all food and beverages are delivered at optimal quality and presentation

Table Maintenance & Service Precision

• Maintain clean, organized, and impeccably presented tables throughout service
• Coordinate closely with food runners and bussers to ensure seamless service execution
• Perform pre-bussing and table maintenance to preserve the dining environment
• Monitor and maintain table settings, glassware, linens, and service details
• Ensure all presentation standards reflect the quality and atmosphere of Cliff House
• Maintain awareness of guest needs while ensuring dining room readiness and efficiency

Guest Relations & Service Recovery

• Respond promptly and professionally to guest questions, concerns, and special requests
• Partner with management to execute service recovery solutions when necessary
• Deliver consistent, personalized service to all guests, including VIPs, members, and tournament participants
• Support special celebrations, private events, and customized guest experiences
• Exercise discretion and professionalism when handling guest concerns

Coordination & Team Collaboration

• Work collaboratively with hosts, food runners, bussers, bartenders, culinarians, and management to ensure exceptional service
• Effectively communicate guest preferences, allergies, dietary restrictions, and special requests
• Participate in pre-shift meetings and team briefings regarding VIP guests, golf events, tournaments, and daily priorities
• Support special functions, member events, and golf-related dining experiences as needed
• Foster a positive team environment focused on operational excellence and guest satisfaction

Financial & Operational Responsibilities

• Accurately process guest checks and complete all financial transactions according to department procedures
• Promote menu items, wine selections, specialty beverages, and featured offerings to drive sales
• Support departmental revenue goals through thoughtful upselling and guest engagement
• Maintain accountability for all transactions, cash handling procedures, and payment processing
• Complete side work, opening duties, and closing responsibilities accurately and efficiently

Compliance & Brand Standards

• Adhere to all Wynn grooming, appearance, and uniform standards
• Follow all health, safety, sanitation, and responsible alcohol service regulations
• Uphold Forbes Five-Star service standards and Wynn’s luxury hospitality expectations
• Execute all responsibilities in accordance with company policies and departmental procedures
• Act as an ambassador of Wynn Las Vegas, Cliff House, and Wynn Golf Club by demonstrating a commitment to luxury hospitality and exceptional guest service

Education & Experience

• High school diploma or equivalent required
• 2–3+ years of experience as a server in a fine dining restaurant, luxury hospitality environment, private club, golf club, or upscale food and beverage operation preferred
• Strong background in upscale dining, wine service, luxury hospitality, or member-focused service environments preferred
• Experience serving high-profile guests, members, or VIP clientele preferred
• Candidates must be at least 21 years of age

Knowledge & Skills

• Advanced knowledge of food, wine, cocktails, and beverage service
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to delivering exceptional guest experiences
• Ability to multitask and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment
• Ability to maintain professionalism and composure under pressure
• Strong sales and guest engagement skills
• Knowledge of luxury hospitality, golf club etiquette, and membership-style service preferred
• Ability to anticipate guest needs and provide personalized recommendations

Licenses & Certifications

• Must be able to obtain and maintain all required work cards and licenses

Work Environment

• Upscale dining restaurant located within the Wynn Golf Club environment
• Luxury guest-facing atmosphere serving golfers, members, resort guests, tournament participants, and VIP patrons
• High-touch service environment requiring constant guest interaction and attention to detail
• Indoor and outdoor-adjacent restaurant setting supporting daily dining operations, golf events, and private functions

jobs.title: Director, Engineering Program Management
jobs.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

At Axon, we build technology that helps Protect Life and address some of society’s most critical safety challenges. Our products combine complex hardware, software, firmware, and manufacturing technologies and are deployed by customers around the world.

As Director of Engineering Program Management, you will lead the Engineering Program Management organization responsible for driving Axon’s Devices products from early concept through development, validation, and launch.

You will lead and develop a team of high-performing Engineering Program Managers who work at the center of Engineering, Product, Design, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, and Operations. Your organization will create the structure, clarity, and accountability that enables cross-functional teams to execute effectively while navigating the technical complexity, ambiguity, and trade-offs inherent in developing world-class products.

Beyond individual program execution, you will own how Engineering Program Management operates across the Devices portfolio. You will help establish development processes, portfolio governance, planning mechanisms, and decision frameworks that allow Axon to scale while maintaining the speed, agility, and ownership required to innovate.

This role requires a leader who can operate at both the strategic and execution levels—someone who can build an exceptional program management organization, partner effectively with senior Engineering and Product leaders, and dive deeply into a critical program when necessary to help teams work through complex technical or execution challenges.

What You’ll Do

Lead the Engineering Program Management Organization

• Lead, develop, and mentor a high-performing team of Engineering Program Managers responsible for complex hardware and connected-device development programs.

• Establish clear expectations for program leadership, execution rigor, communication, risk management, and cross-functional accountability.

• Build organizational capability through coaching, hiring, talent development, and succession planning.

• Foster a culture of ownership, transparency, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Own Portfolio-Level Program Execution

• Oversee execution of the Devices product development portfolio from early concept through product launch.

• Maintain visibility across program schedules, dependencies, risks, budgets, resources, and major development milestones.

• Identify systemic risks and cross-program dependencies early and drive resolution with Engineering, Product, and Operations leadership.

• Establish mechanisms that provide leadership with clear, objective visibility into portfolio health and enable timely decision-making.

• Step into critical programs when necessary to help teams resolve ambiguity, remove roadblocks, and establish a credible path forward.

Drive Product Development Excellence

• Own and continuously evolve the program management processes and operating mechanisms used to develop Axon Devices products.

• Establish scalable development frameworks that provide appropriate rigor and governance without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

• Drive consistent execution of phase-gate, build-readiness, risk-management, change-control, and launch-readiness processes.

• Partner with Engineering leaders to continually improve how teams plan, make decisions, manage dependencies, and execute complex product development.

Lead Cross-Functional Alignment

• Partner closely with leaders across Hardware Engineering, Firmware, Software, Industrial Design, Product Management, Supply Chain, Quality, and Operations.

• Ensure teams are aligned on program objectives, priorities, requirements, development plans, and key trade-offs.

• Create clarity where ownership or priorities are ambiguous and facilitate decisions that allow teams to maintain momentum.

• Build strong relationships across functions and influence outcomes even where direct organizational authority does not exist.

Manage Portfolio Priorities and Resources

• Partner with Engineering and Product leadership to translate product strategy into executable development plans.

• Evaluate resource needs and constraints across the portfolio and help leadership make informed prioritization and investment decisions.

• Identify conflicts between programs and drive decisions around sequencing, resources, schedules, and scope.

• Balance speed, technical risk, customer needs, quality, cost, and organizational capacity when evaluating program trade-offs.

Own Financial and Program Planning

• Oversee program operating and capital budgets across the Devices development portfolio.

• Establish disciplined forecasting and budget-management practices across the EPM organization.

• Partner with Engineering, Finance, and Product leadership on resource planning, investment decisions, and portfolio forecasts.

• Ensure program teams understand both the technical and business implications of development decisions.

Drive Executive Communication and Decision-Making

• Provide clear, concise, and objective communication to senior and executive leadership regarding portfolio health, key risks, decisions, and trade-offs.

• Ensure risks and issues are surfaced early, with clear ownership and actionable paths toward resolution.

• Distill complex technical and cross-functional issues into the information necessary for effective leadership decisions.

• Facilitate difficult decisions where technical, schedule, financial, customer, and business priorities compete.

What You Bring

• 12+ years of relevant experience in engineering program management, technical program management, product development, or related roles, with significant experience developing complex hardware products.

• 5+ years of people leadership experience, including building, developing, and leading high-performing program management teams.

• Demonstrated experience leading multiple complex hardware or connected-device programs from concept through production launch.

• Strong understanding of hardware product development, including electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, firmware/software integration, validation, manufacturing, and new product introduction.

• Deep program management expertise across schedule development, risk management, resource planning, budget management, development milestones, and cross-functional execution.

• Experience developing and scaling product development processes, governance models, and operating mechanisms across an organization.

• Demonstrated ability to manage a portfolio of programs and make thoughtful prioritization and resource trade-offs.

• Strong business and financial acumen, including experience managing significant development budgets and capital investments.

• Proven ability to influence across organizational boundaries and align diverse technical and business teams around a common objective.

• Ability to operate effectively in ambiguity, create clarity, and drive decisions in a fast-moving product development environment.

• Ability to understand complex technical issues, ask the right questions, and communicate implications effectively to both engineering teams and executive leadership.

• Exceptional judgment, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to balance technical, schedule, cost, quality, and customer considerations.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including demonstrated effectiveness communicating with senior and executive leadership.

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience developing high-volume consumer electronics, connected devices, cameras, communications products, or similarly complex hardware systems.

• Experience working with global manufacturing, CM/JDM, and supply-chain partners.

• Experience operating in a fast-growing organization where product development processes and organizational structures are evolving.

• Experience managing products that combine hardware, firmware, software, cloud connectivity, and manufacturing complexity.

Benefits that Benefit You

• Competitive salary and 401k with employer match

• Discretionary paid time off

• Paid parental leave for all

• Medical, Dental, Vision plans

• Fitness Programs

• Emotional & Mental Wellness support

• Learning & Development programs

• And yes, we have snacks in our offices

Axon and all Axon-affiliated entities are Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employers. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Important Notes

The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions.

Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment.

We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at axongreenhousesupport@axon.com or via our Axon Privacy Web Form. For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice.

Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment.

We are an equal opportunity employer that promotes justice, advances equity, values diversity and fosters inclusion. We’re committed to hiring the best talent — regardless of race, creed, color, ancestry, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances — and empowering all of our employees so they can do their best work. If you have a disability or special need that requires assistance or accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email recruitingops@axon.com.  Please note that this email address is for accommodation purposes only. Axon will not respond to inquiries for other purposes.

We do not make job offers via text message, WhatsApp, or instant messaging platforms without a formal interview process.  All legitimate job openings are listed on our official careers page at https://www.axon.com/careers.  If you receive a suspicious offer or outreach from an email address that is not @axon.com, or if you are asked for sensitive personal information (bank details, Social Security Number) prematurely, please ignore the message and report it to recruitingops@axon.com.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Fulfillment
jobs.description:
About Faire

Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

About this role

Fulfillment is one of Faire's top long-term strategic bets that fundamentally changes how both brands and retailers do business. You'll play an instrumental role in scaling Faire's fulfillment business from 1% to 20%+ of GMV, working across the full problem space of brand supply, retailer demand, and unit economics to build the products and operational foundations that make Faire the best way for brands to fulfill wholesale and the most flexible, valuable way for retailers to stock their stores.

The product problems you'll tackle are both digital and physical in nature, spanning marketplace dynamics, operational systems, and program economics. You'll partner cross-functionally and with senior fulfillment leads to drive end-to-end execution and strategy on key workstreams touching brands, retailers, and operations.

We're looking for a product manager with deep empathy for how our customers' businesses actually work, relentless execution in ambiguous 0→1 environments, and the instinct to always connect what they're building to why it matters for the broader business.

What you’ll do

• Brand supply. Build onboarding, sales enablement, and operational tooling that makes it easier and more compelling for brands to fulfill through Faire, with a deep understanding of what it actually takes for a brand to change how they operate.

• Retailer demand. Drive 50%+ growth to participating brands through Faire Source by closing the discovery, conversion, and cart experience gaps that hold retailers back from making it their primary way to buy.

• Fulfillment experience. Build toward 90%+ of Faire-fulfilled orders being perfectly delivered, while identifying the net new levers that make fulfillment a genuine differentiator on both sides of the marketplace.

• Unit economics. Partner with S&A and operations to generate leverage and halve the cost of fulfillment as we scale, from order batching and 3PL collaboration to brand consolidation.

• Cross-functional execution. Work in close partnership with engineering, design, operations, GTM, finance, and data science to ship end-to-end — defining success metrics and communicating progress, tradeoffs, and decisions clearly across the org.

Qualifications

• Business empathy. You understand how your customers' businesses actually work, not just their user flows. Fulfillment asks brands and retailers to make fundamental operational changes; you grasp those stakes and can navigate the marketplace tradeoffs when their interests intersect.

• Cross-functional execution. You relentlessly chase down problems across eng, ops, design, analytics, and GTM. You earn trust quickly, lead without authority, and work in lockstep with a fast-moving team.

• Systems thinking. You understand how your work fits into the broader puzzle. You don't build shopping experiences without thinking about unit economics, or build brand tooling without thinking about ops partnership.

• Structured problem solving. You systematically break down hard problems and bring creativity and resourcefulness to finding durable solutions.

• Analytical depth. You're fluent in business equations and experimental data. You go deeper than the first answer, whether that's "what's the best way to rank products on this page" or "what's preventing brands from sending inventory correctly."

• Learning velocity. You thrive in fast-paced, 0→1 environments where the problem space is evolving. You get meaningfully better each month and grow alongside the problem space. You don't need to be told twice.

jobs.title: Mechanisms Engineer
jobs.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast is looking for a Mechanisms Engineer, reporting to the Sr. Manager of Mechanisms, to support the development of space mechanisms.

This will be a full-time, exempt position located in our Long Beach location.

Responsibilities:

• Develop mechanisms from ideation to flight: design, analyze, build, test, and iteration. Some mechanisms include motorized assemblies, linkages, spring/damper systems, rotating hardware, and crew-operated assemblies

• Own critical spacecraft hardware/systems, assuming profound responsibility for their hardware

• Interface with a world-class production team to ensure successful translation of designs into spacecraft

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, or similar engineering

• 2+ years of experience in the design, build, and/or test of mechanisms, structures, valves, or other mechanical systems

Preferred Skills & Experience:

• Thriving in a team that emphasizes rapid prototyping, quick iteration, and a general bias towards action

• Strong understanding of spacecraft and/or launch vehicle mechanisms and mechanical assemblies

• Experience in NX/Teamcenter or other CAD packages (PTC Creo, CATIA) with a solid understanding and application of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) per ASME Y14.5

• Professional or project experience with FEMAP, ANSYS, or similar finite element analysis (FEA) software tools, as well as a good understanding of fatigue, fracture, and crack propagation

• Knowledge of metallic manufacturing techniques, processes, equipment, and other processes such as machining, welding, riveting, bending, assembling, etc.

• Good understanding and experience working with aerospace materials (metals, plastics, composites)

• Solid understanding of test methods/setups and data acquisition systems

• Ability to perform trade studies using first principles and engineering fundamentals to make clear recommendations even with partial information

• Passion for advancing the commercial space industry and human spaceflight

• Able to work well in an integrated collaborative team environment, including frequent interactions with technicians, other engineers, managers, and support teams

• Highly self-motivated with strong organizational and written/oral communication skills – able to prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment with the ongoing drive for continuous improvement in all aspects of work

Additional Requirements:

• Up to 10% travel to remote sites and vendors as needed

Pay Range: California

$112,340—$230,000 USD

We calibrate level and compensation to the selected candidate's experience and demonstrated capability. We welcome applicants across a range of experience levels to apply.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Base salary will vary depending on job-related knowledge, education, skills, experience, business needs, and market demand. Salary is just one component of our comprehensive compensation package. Full-time employees also receive company equity, as well as access to a full suite of compelling benefits and perks, including: medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, generous paid time off; up to 20+ days of vacation for exempt staff and up to 10+ days of vacation for non-exempt staff with the ability to cash-out unused vacation annually, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, ClassPass credits, personalized mental healthcare through Spring Health, and other discounts and perks. We also take pride in offering exceptional food perks, with snacks, drip coffee & onsite barista, cold drinks, and dinner meals remaining free of charge, and lunch subsidized as part of Vast’s ongoing commitment to providing high-quality meals for employees.

U.S. EXPORT CONTROL COMPLIANCE STATUS

The person hired will have access to information and items subject to U.S. export controls, and therefore, must either be a “U.S. person” as defined by 22 C.F.R. § 120.62 or otherwise eligible for deemed export licensing. This status includes U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, lawful permanent residents (green card holders), and asylees and refugees with such status granted, not pending.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, apply online. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. You should possess navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area and must be able to navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

Operate all equipment.

Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

Prepare product.

Receive and process telephone orders.

Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

Must be able to make correct monetary change.

Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

Fumes from food odors.

Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

Depth perception.

Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile bricks with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36 and 48.

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72 high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing walking and climbing duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24 - 30 and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Additional Job Details

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72 occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

jobs.title: FSQA Manager
jobs.description:
The FSQA Manager, Technical Services serves as the technical authority for ingredient commercialization, supplier qualification, specification management, and product quality performance. This role leads complex innovation, renovation, supply continuity, and supplier onboarding projects from concept through full-scale implementation. The position partners cross-functionally with Product Development, Procurement, Supply Chain Operations, Marketing, Regulatory, and suppliers to help ensure ingredients meet food safety, quality, regulatory, operational, and brand standards.

What You’ll Do

• Lead end-to-end commercialization activities for new ingredients, suppliers, and product renovation initiatives from concept through full-scale implementation.
• Serve as the technical authority for supplier qualification and approval, scale-up activities, troubleshooting, plant trials and validation, product evaluations, risk assessment and mitigation, project management, timeline management, specifications, and technical standards.
• Lead complex innovation, renovation, supply continuity, supplier onboarding, and ingredient qualification projects that support innovation and supply chain initiatives.
• Review, create, and modify ingredient and supplier specifications, including product attributes, analytical measures, and technical standards.
• Partner on cross-functional teams as a subject matter expert, communicating the impact of changes to leadership and supporting ingredient quality and brand standards.
• Identify and lead implementation of process improvements that enhance quality, consistency, cost optimization, and development processes, including SOPs, specifications, and procedures.
• Lead food safety and quality assurance activities related to ingredient commercialization, supplier qualification, product evaluations, and technical standards while identifying system gaps and implementing risk-reduction solutions.
• Guide, develop, and oversee plans for consumer and analytical product testing to support product evaluation and decision-making.

• Bachelor’s degree in Food Science or a related field, or equivalent experience and expertise.
• Minimum 10 years of experience in Food Safety & Quality Assurance or Product Development, preferably within the QSR industry.
• Relevant food safety certification or equivalent, such as ServSafe, HACCP, IFT, Food Analysis, Food Testing, Food Processing, Lean Manufacturing, or similar evidence of continued education.
• Strong knowledge of test plan development, data collection, statistical analysis, and data summarization, with the ability to communicate findings and recommendations to leadership.
• Strong analytical, presentation, written, and verbal communication skills with outstanding attention to detail.
• Proven background in food manufacturing, quality management, food safety, and manufacturing troubleshooting.
• Advanced problem-solving and decision-making skills.

jobs.title: Customer Service Rep(08544) - 3388 Palm Ave.
jobs.description:
Job Duties
• Operate all equipment. • Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler. • Prepare product. • Receive and process telephone orders. • Take inventory and complete associated paperwork. • Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.
Training
Orientation and training provided on the job.
Communication Skills
Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions. Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.
Essential Functions/Skills
Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator). Must be able to make correct monetary change.
Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed. Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.
Work Conditions
EXPOSURE TO: Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks. In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas. Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside. Fumes from food odors. Exposure to cornmeal dust. Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler. Hot surfaces/tools from over up to 500 degrees or higher. Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.
SENSING: Talking and hearing on the telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks. Depth perception. Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.
TEMPERMENTS: The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work along and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.
STANDING: Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile “bricks” with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36” and 48”.
WALKING: Walking is generally in short distances for short durations.
Delivery personnel must travel between the store and the delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer’s location.
SITTING: Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or
table.
LIFTING: Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck. Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3’ x 1.5’. Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacking onto shelves up to 72” high.
CARRYING: Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves. Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried form the storage room to the front of the store. Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.
During delivery, carry pizzas, sides, and beverages while performing “walking” and “climbing” duties.
DRIVING: Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A team member may make several deliveries per shift.
PUSHING: Pushing is performed to move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24”-30” and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push. Trays may also be pulled.
CLIMBING: Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.
During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of
stairs may be required.
STOOPING/BENDING: Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station. Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station. Duration of this position is approximately 40-45 seconds at a time, repeated continuously during the day. Forward bending is also present at the front counter when stocking ingredients.
CROUCHING/SQUATTING: Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.
REACHING: Reaching is performed continuously; up, down, and forward. Workers reach above 72” occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves. Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes. Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.
HAND TASKS: Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day. Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists. Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing a pizza from an the oven., and when using the rolling cutter. Frequent
and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes. Team members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

MACHINE, TOOLS, EQUIPMENT, WORK AIDS: Team members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer II, Advanced Product Development
jobs.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form's Advanced Product Development team is responsible for architecting and designing the next generation of our iron-air battery system — the cell, module, pack, and the support systems that keep them running reliably for decades in the field. We work ahead of our production programs, translating breakthrough electrochemistry and system requirements into mechanical designs that can scale to high-volume manufacturing.



We're hiring a Mechanical Engineer II to support the design, build and test hardware for our next generation of iron-air batteries. As part of our Advanced Product Development team, you will have a hands-on role in designing next-generation system-level designs. You will also have the opportunity to design parts for volume manufacturing. Your work will rely on a broad range of engineering disciplines, including heat transfer, fluid dynamics and mechanics. You will integrate tightly with a team of experienced engineers to write and execute verification test plans and iterate on designs with data-driven analysis. You’ll be a part of a large cross-functional team bringing Energy Storage Systems from concept to release to mass manufacturing. This is an exciting opportunity to deliver our sustainable multi-day energy storage solution to the grid!



Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Lead hands-on prototyping and verification testing of subsystem designs.

 - Drive instrumentation, data collection and data analysis for system-level validation builds.

 - Own design of components and assemblies for volume manufacturing.

 - Run and analyze trials to inform specs and future design direction.

 - Execute ambitious product development processes on tight timelines.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field; Bachelor's with 1+ years experience in mechanical design, or Master's with research or professional engineering experience.

 - Experienced using CAD to design parts and assemblies.

 - Exposure to writing, executing and analyzing test plans to make data-driven decisions.

 - Experience with prototyping techniques and working in a lab environment.

 - Strong heat transfer, fluid dynamics and mechanics fundamentals.



#LI-Onsite



Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here. 



When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed. 



To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.




If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.

Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will never solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.

Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, drop us a line. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From customer service representative to management, General Manager to Manager Corporate Operations or Franchisee, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

JOB REQUIREMENTS

You must be 16 years of age or older.

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 4".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

· Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

· Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

· Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

· Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

· Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

· Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

· To move trays which are placed on dollies.

· A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

· Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

· Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

· Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

· Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

· Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

· Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

· Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

· Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

· Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

· Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

· Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

· Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

· Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

· Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

jobs.title: Core Strategy Senior Lead
jobs.location: New York City, NY; San Francisco, CA
jobs.description:
About Faire

Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

About this role

The Core Strategy team reports directly to our CEO and is tasked with solving some of Faire’s most urgent and challenging problems. This can range from driving investment decisions on major expansion opportunities to directly owning pilot execution on high potential new bets. We operate at a wide range of altitudes and across all areas of the business.

You will be joining a small team with a high degree of autonomy and responsibility. The work will vary project-to-project, but the throughline is that you will be taking ambiguous, complex problems, creating clarity, and then driving to impact. In many cases that will mean you are directly owning outcomes for high priority pilots or other initiatives. As an example, our team drove the decision to launch Faire Source and then played a central role in building the program from the ground up alongside a small cross-functional team.

This role combines strategic thinking, analytical rigor, product judgment, external & internal relationship-building, and the operational chops to get things done. We are looking for someone who is equally at home unpacking ambiguous board-level strategy questions as they are running a scrappy pilot. No matter the project, success in this role will always look like creating clarity and then seeing that clarity through to real-world impact.

What you’ll do

• Take ambiguous, high-stakes problems from first framing through to implementation

• Break down complex questions from first principles, with a mix of analytical rigor, customer insight, and collaboration with internal and external experts

• Consistently raise the bar on how our team uses AI to get to better answers, faster

• Collaborate closely with the product, analytics, marketing, finance, and ops teams to solve problems and drive through execution to outcomes

• Spot cross-functional dependencies early and unblock them yourself

• Present your recommendations and debate their implications with Faire’s executive team, guiding key company decisions

• Help shape the culture and capabilities of the Core Strategy team by improving our processes, mentoring teammates, and setting a high bar for excellence

Qualifications

• A Bachelor’s degree and 8+ years of experience across consulting, business operations, product, strategy, or analytics roles

• Exceptional problem solving skills and ability to identify and synthesize insights from data

• Deep analytical toolkit, with strong proficiency in Excel, SQL, and AI tools

• Executive-level communication skills, including the ability to use verbal and written communication to express ideas clearly and succinctly

• Excellent at breaking down unstructured problems and synthesizing many disparate sources of information to deliver simple and thoughtful answers

• Strong business judgment, with ability to think across every dimension of the business

• Experience with quantitative and qualitative consumer and market research techniques

• Ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy and ownership

• Curiosity, low ego, and willingness to learn from a wide range of people

Salary Range

San Francisco or New York City: the pay range for this role is $197,500 - $271,500 per year.

This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors such as transferable skills, work experience, market demands, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

Hybrid Faire employees currently go into the office 3 days per week on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and a third flex day of their choosing (Monday, Wednesday, or Friday). Additionally, hybrid in-office roles will have the flexibility to work remotely up to 4 weeks per year. Specific Workplace and Information Technology positions may require onsite attendance 5 days per week as will be indicated in the job posting.

Why you’ll love working at Faire

• Move fast: You'll own meaningful problems that serve customers around the globe with the agency to move fast and see your results clearly.

• Equipped to scale: We invest in what matters, including the latest enterprise AI tools, to help you work smarter and get more out of every day.

• Best in class: Our team is full of sharp, kind, and generous colleagues who care about their craft and about helping you grow in yours.

• Real rewards. Competitive pay, equity, and comprehensive benefits designed to support your life inside and outside of work.

• Belonging: We're intentional about building an environment where every Faire employee has equal access to opportunities, growth, and success.

Faire was founded in 2017 by a team of early product and engineering leads from Square. We’re backed by some of the top investors in retail and tech including: Y Combinator, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Forerunner Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, and DST Global. We have headquarters in San Francisco and Kitchener-Waterloo, and a global employee presence across offices in Toronto, London, and New York. To learn more about Faire and our customers, you can read more on our blog.

Faire provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression.

Faire is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process and applicants with a disability may request to be accommodated throughout the recruitment process. We will work with all applicants to accommodate their individual accessibility needs.  To request reasonable accommodation, please fill out our Accommodation Request Form (https://bit.ly/faire-form)

Privacy

For information about the type of personal data Faire collects from applicants, as well as your choices regarding the data collected about you, please visit Faire’s Privacy Notice (https://www.faire.com/privacy)
