jobs.title: Senior Manager, Population Health
jobs.description:
About Us

Greenbrook Medical is building the new standard in primary care.

We deliver high-touch, relationship-based care through neighborhood clinics, grounded in a simple belief: every senior deserves the kind of care we would want for our own families. Our model prioritizes time with patients, strong care coordination, and a personalized approach that improves outcomes while lowering total cost of care.

We take full accountability for patient outcomes and overall cost of care, aligning clinical excellence with disciplined execution. That commitment shows up in our results, including a patient Net Promoter Score of 91, compared to 32 for typical healthcare organizations.

Rooted in Tampa Bay and partnered with Tampa General Hospital, we are entering an exciting phase of growth. Backed by strong unit economics, experienced operators, and a proven playbook, we are looking for builders and operators who want to help scale a healthcare platform designed to deliver better care, better coordination, and better outcomes for seniors.

About The Role

Greenbrook takes full financial risk on the health of our patients, so a handful of drivers determine whether the model works: how often our patients need the hospital, how well we manage specialty and pharmacy spend, and how completely we capture the health of the people we care for. Getting these right is the difference between a model that works at four clinics and one that works at forty.

As a member of the Population Health team, you make sure our performance scales, and will own on one of our important drivers (Part A, Part B, Part D, Revenue). You work hand in hand with the leader who runs that function to build the workflows and tools they need to manage their lever. This is a highly visible role with direct impact on the drivers that determine whether the model works.

As Senior Manager, Population Health, you own four things:

• The driver metrics: you know what moves performance on your driver and you are accountable for moving the metrics behind it. You partner with analytics engineering to define those metrics, propose what good looks like with your functional leader, and make the driver observable

• The processes behind it: documenting how the work runs today, finding where it breaks down, and designing improvements alongside the clinical and operational leaders who own the workflow

• The tooling: you build functional first versions and pilot them with the teams you support, then partner with engineering and product to build the durable version

• The roadmap: you find and size the opportunities in your area and put the near-term roadmap together with your functional leader, for approval by Pop Health leadership

The surface area is wide. One driver spans several clinical and operational processes, multiple teams across every clinic, and the tooling and reporting underneath all of it.

This is a high-autonomy role, so you have real agency to find the work and shape the roadmap in partnership with the function you support. You work hand in hand with the leader who runs that function, and you report to the Head of Population Health and AI Enablement.

Location: New York City strongly preferred (Hybrid). Open to exceptional remote candidates.

What You'll Do

Make Your Driver Visible

• Define the metrics that show how your driver is performing, propose what good looks like, and partner with analytics engineering to get them into production reporting

• Build the reporting and observability that let the function see performance in time to act on it

• Use the data to show your functional leader where to focus

Improve the Processes With the People Who Own Them

• Embed in the work: sit in the meetings, shadow the people running the process, document how it operates and build deep relationships with operators

• Find where the process breaks down, quantify what it costs, and design the improvement with the clinical and operational leaders who own that workflow

• Pilot, iterate, and support launch and training, with the leader accountable for the outcome bought in and sponsoring the change

• Build the documentation and tooling that keep an improved process consistent as we open new clinics

Build the Tooling

• Take what the process needs, from tooling and from observability, and build it: internal applications and interfaces that surface the right work to the right person, pull live cost and risk data, and capture what happened. You will use agentic coding tools to ship these yourself

• Run structured vendor evaluations and bring a build-versus-buy recommendation

• Represent your driver in the major platform builds, from defining the business requirements through deployment and adoption in the clinics

Shape the Roadmap with Your Function

• Size the opportunities in your area and propose the near-term roadmap with your functional leader each quarter, with a clear definition of done for each initiative

• Keep the committed work on track, and adjust course when the facts change

What Success Looks Like

• Driver Metrics: your driver metrics improve against the targets set with your functional leader, and you can explain why

• Observability: your area's performance is visible in production reporting, trusted by the people who use it, and available before decisions have to be made

• Delivery: the initiatives you committed to for the quarter shipped and got used

• Functional Partnership: the leader you support would tell us their function runs better because you are in it

• Adoption: the improvements you build get used, and they hold as new clinics open

• Metrics you'll own: your driver metrics, delivery against committed quarterly initiatives, and counterpart satisfaction among the leaders in your area

About You

We encourage strong performers from a range of backgrounds to apply. People come to this work from analytics and from operations, and we do not expect depth in both on day one.

You bring:

• 4 to 8 years of experience, ideally including time at a value-based care or multi-site provider organization

• Depth from one of two directions: either a product or engineering background where you have built and shipped working tools yourself, or market operations / BizOps experience where you have designed workflows alongside clinical leaders

• A track record of owning ambiguous work and seeing it through, including work nobody had defined before you got there

• Comfort working directly with data: pulling and analyzing in SQL, and reading a schema well enough to know where the answer lives

• Bachelor's degree required

• A mindset grounded in our core values of Heart, Excellence, Accountability, Resilience, and Teamwork

You'll stand out if you:

• Get to root cause: a strong first-principles thinker who can look at a broken process or a confusing dataset and work out what is actually driving the problem, rather than accepting how it gets described

• Operate with high agency: you make progress without waiting for the work to be defined for you, and you run toward the problems you identify and take ownership of them

• Earn trust on the front line: you understand a workflow before you redesign it, and the people running it want you in the room

• Build relationships from scratch: you create your own mandate across functions rather than waiting for one

• Are AI-native: you live in modern AI tools to support your work

• Communicate with clarity: the same clarity with a care manager, a physician, and the leadership team

• Own the outcome: high bias for action, follow through on commitments, and close loops without needing to be chased

Why You'll Love Working Here

Make An Impact Every Day

Be part of a mission-driven team transforming primary care for seniors. Your work directly supports better outcomes, better coordination, and better experiences for some of the most vulnerable patients in healthcare.

Work That Actually Matters

We're not a volume-driven system, we're accountable for outcomes. That means your work directly contributes to quality care, patient satisfaction, and meaningful improvements in how healthcare is delivered.

Build And Grow With Us

We're building more than a company, we're building careers. As we expand, you'll have opportunities to grow your skills and take on new challenges.

Strong, Transparent Compensation & Benefits

• $150,000 annually, based on experience and qualifications

• Generous annual performance bonus

• Health, dental, and vision insurance

• Paid time off

• 401(k) with company match

Our Selection Process

Application → Initial interview → Skills/experience interview → Values interview → Case Study and Case Study Interview → References

Equal Employment Opportunity and Commitment to Diversity

At Greenbrook Medical, we believe the only way we accomplish our mission is by building the best team in healthcare. We do this through a culture of respect and belonging, ensuring our teammates feel cared for first and foremost.

We will extend equal employment opportunity to all applicants without regard to age, race, ethnicity, sex, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, socioeconomic background, disability status, military affiliation, pregnancy or any other status protected under federal, state and local laws. We encourage all who share our mission to apply. Greenbrook Medical will provide reasonable accommodations during the recruitment process. If you need additional accommodations or assistance, do not hesitate to contact our People team at recruiting@greenbrookmedical.com.

jobs.title: Associate General Counsel, Product & Regulatory
jobs.location: North America l San Francisco, CA or Cambridge, MA
jobs.description:
Liquid AI is an efficiency-first foundation model company. We build highly capable AI models designed to operate across the full range of environments—from cloud infrastructure to phones, vehicles, and other edge devices.


OPPORTUNITY

Liquid AI is seeking an experienced Associate General Counsel to lead our product counseling and AI regulatory work.

Reporting to the Chief Legal Officer, this person will work closely with our product, research, and engineering teams as they develop and deploy new AI models and products. The role requires someone who can understand novel and unsettled legal issues, make practical decisions, and translate those decisions into things the company can actually do.

The job is not simply to monitor regulatory developments or write policies. It is to determine what they mean for Liquid’s products and help the company act.


CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own legal support for the development, release, and deployment of Liquid’s models and products.

 - Advise product, research, and engineering teams on AI regulation, privacy, data use, intellectual property, model safety, security, and product claims.

 - Lead Liquid’s response to the EU AI Act and other emerging AI laws, including the practical controls, documentation, and product decisions needed for compliance.

 - Advise on training and evaluation data, synthetic data, model outputs, open-source and open-weight releases, fine-tuning, and customer deployments.

 - Support the commercial team on product and regulatory issues arising in strategic customer and partnership agreements.


REQUIRED CAPABILITIES

 - At least 8 years of relevant legal experience, including meaningful in-house experience advising technology product teams.

 - Strong background in AI regulation, privacy, data governance, intellectual property, or related technology issues.

 - Ability to understand how Liquid’s products work and give clear, practical, risk-based advice.

 - Ability to operate independently, identify issues before they become problems, and drive work through completion.

 - Comfort making decisions in areas where the law is new, unsettled, or simply does not provide a clean answer.

 - Clear, concise writing.


THE RIGHT CANDIDATE

 - Thinks from first principles and is genuinely interested in technology.

 - Wants to work directly with the people building products—not review them from a distance.

 - Exercises judgment rather than reflexively escalating, documenting, or avoiding risk.

 - Is comfortable taking ownership, being decisive, and occasionally being wrong.

 - High integrity, optimistic, and low ego.

 - Healthy sense of humor.

jobs.title: Strategy & Operations Manager, Communications
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Communications team is responsible for helping people understand our mission, technology, and impact. The team works across the company to communicate clearly and thoughtfully with a wide range of audiences in a rapidly evolving environment.

Within Communications, the Strategy & Systems team is building a new model for how communications organizations operate—combining strong strategic judgment, effective operating systems, and the growing capabilities of AI. We design the frameworks, tools, and ways of working that help the broader team focus on its highest-impact priorities and execute them effectively.



About the Role

We are looking for a Strategy & Operations Manager to help make this operating model real. You will translate priorities into action, lead high-impact initiatives from idea through implementation, and design better ways for the Communications team to work.

You will take ownership of complex projects that require clear thinking, strong follow-through, and a willingness to challenge how work has traditionally been done. You will partner with senior leaders, technical builders, and cross-functional teams to bring structure to ambiguous problems, strengthen execution, and apply AI in practical ways that improve how the organization operates.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.



In this role, you will:

 - Lead strategic initiatives and special projects across Communications, turning ambiguous opportunities into clearly defined problems, aligned plans, and successful implementation.

 - Help shape how the team sets priorities, makes decisions, and follows through on its most important work—including launches, campaigns, reactive moments, and longer-term initiatives.

 - Design an AI-forward approach to project and program management, building systems that maintain momentum, surface risks early, and make ownership and dependencies clear.

 - Build operating rhythms, planning frameworks, and shared processes that create clarity without adding unnecessary meetings, manual tracking, or layers of coordination.

 - Translate emerging AI capabilities into practical workflows that reduce repetitive work, strengthen coordination, and allow team members to focus on work that most benefits from human judgment.

jobs.title: EHS Manager
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world’s transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people’s quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables.

Job Summary

As an Environment Health and Safety (EHS) Manager your primary emphasis will be to lead a diverse team in an operational setting promoting a culture of safety, sustainability and environmental responsibility.  You will be responsible for developing and implementing industrial safety, laboratory safety, industrial hygiene, and environmental programs, managing regulatory compliance and fostering a safe and environmentally conscious work environment.

You will manage a cross functional EHS team in a growing environment covering several phases, such as research and development, manufacturing, construction, and operations.  You and your team are responsible for the overall health and safety of the facility.

A successful candidate will need to be highly collaborative, have a lean business mindset, be able to find pioneering ways to achieve complex objectives, adaptable to a fast moving environment, be able to prioritize objectives, and align with the company’s goals and risk tolerance.

Responsibilities

• Lead a diverse team of EHS professionals, while providing mentorship and growth opportunities.

• Develop, implement and maintain environmental, health and safety programs to ensure compliance with local, state and federal regulations.

• Partner with operations, maintenance, laboratory, construction, and research staff to ensure proper identification and mitigation of hazards to ensure work gets done safely.

• Drive the Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) process to improve the overall safety of operations.

• Strategize and implement plans to reduce incident rates and improve EHS performance.

• Implement emergency response plans for incidents and ensure employees are trained accordingly.

• Develops, reviews and conducts EHS-related training, including safety orientation, as part of the new hire orientation meetings.

• Promote a culture of environmental responsibility and encourage sustainable practices throughout the organization.

• Stay current with all environmental, health and safety regulations, inspections and standards and ensure the organization's adherence to all applicable laws.

• Prepare, maintain and submit regulatory reports, permits and documentation as required.

• Conduct workplace inspections and audits to monitor compliance and to identify areas for improvement.

• Oversee hazardous material program including inventory, disposal, recycling, and handling.

• Partner and manage relationships with vendors to assist with the environment, health and safety of the facility.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams, management and external agencies to ensure alignment with safety goals.

• Ensure that EHS is providing opportunities for direct and honest communication including leading safety committee meetings, toolbox talks, lunch and learns, safety moments, etc.

• Maintains regular engagement with employees and operational areas to understand workflow and operational processes, identify emerging risks and support EHS solutions.

• Investigate all incidents and accidents, determining root causes and implementing corrective and preventive measures.

• Maintain incident records and report findings to upper management and regulatory authorities as required through the First Report of Incident process.

• Collect, analyze and report data related to safety performance.

• Identify trends and opportunities for improvement based on data analysis.

• Drive results through the Objectives and Key Results (OKR) process, while leveraging partnerships with key contributors.

• Be a first responder and part of Emergency Response Team.

• Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Occupational Health and Safety, or a related field.

• 5+ years of management of EHS programs focusing on safety management, regulatory compliance, risk management, and program development.

• 5+ years of direct management experience.

• Must have expertise in a discipline within EHS, certification is preferred.

• Proven track record in working with others to accomplish objectives.

• Proven track record of developing a strong safety culture and reducing recordable incident rates.

• Professional certification relevant to EHS, such as Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Certified Industrial Hygienist (CHI), Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM), or another relevant credential is preferred but not required.

• Experience supporting EHS activities across multiple operating environments, such as research and development, laboratories, manufacturing, construction, and facility operations is preferred but not required.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

• In-depth understanding of local, state and federal EH&S regulations applicable to the industry.

• Knowledge of recognized hazard-identification, risk-assessment and control methodologies, including Job Hazard Analysis and the hierarchy of controls.

• Knowledge of incident-investigation and root-cause-analysis principles and corrective-action practices.

• Ability to develop, implement, evaluate, and continuously improve EHS programs, procedures and management systems.

• Ability to assess complex or changing work processes and recommend practical, risk-based EHS controls.

• Ability to interpret regulatory requirements and communicate their operational implications to employees and management.

• Ability to analyze EHS data and performance metrics, identify trends and develop appropriate improvement strategies.

• Ability to lead, coach and develop EHS professionals and establish clear priorities and accountability.

• Ability to build collaborative working relationships across operational, technical, research, maintenance, construction, and management functions.

• Ability to influence decisions and promote safe work practices without relying solely on direct authority.

• Ability to communicate technical EHS information clearly through written procedures, reports, presentations, training, and employee engagement.

• Ability to manage multiple EHS priorities in a dynamic R&D and operational environment, while applying sound judgment to risk-based decisions.

• Ability to lead or support emergency preparedness and response activities within the scope of assigned training and responsibilities.

• Ability to engage employees at all organizational levels and encourage reporting, participation and continuous improvement in EHS programs.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

• Capability to conduct thorough incident investigations and risk assessments.

• Strong knowledge of EHS regulations, codes and standards.

• Excellent communication, leadership and interpersonal skills.

• Prioritizes and ensures safety of oneself and others.

• Ability to proactively collect, manage and transfer knowledge.

• Ability to seek different and novel ways to create efficiencies when working on problems, challenges and issues.

Physical Demands

• Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, scissor lifts, articulated boom lifts, etc..

• Setting up and transferring temporary structures (e.g. scaffolding, ladders).

• Moving self in different positions to accomplish tasks in various environments, including tight and confined spaces.

• Remaining in a stationary position, often standing or sitting for prolonged periods.

• Moving about to accomplish tasks or moving from one worksite to another.

• Adjusting, moving, transporting, installing, positioning, or removing objects up to 35 pounds in all directions.

Environmental Conditions

• General office environment.

• Low temperatures.

• High temperatures.

• Outdoor environment or elements, such as precipitation and wind.

• Noisy environments.

• Small and/or enclosed spaces.

• Odors or fumes from chemicals or chemical reactions.

• Elevated heights.

Safety and PPE

• Manipulating, cleaning and disposal of hazardous materials.

• Reporting issues with equipment or unsafe conditions.

• Wearing proper PPE, to include face mask, face shields, gloves, safety shoes, etc..

• Handling of Beryllium (Be) containing material.

Travel

• Some travel may be required, up to 10%.

Certification

• Professional certification relevant to EHS, such as Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Certified Industrial Hygienist (CHI), Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM), or another relevant credential is preferred but not required.

Additional Requirements

• Seldom requires working weekends.

• Occasionally requires schedule flexibility.

• Seldom requires non-standard work-week hours.

• Seldom requires extended hours to support launch and critical project timelines.

• Onsite: #LI-Onsite

About our Benefits

We know that we have some of the most talented and dedicated employees, and we believe in rewarding them accordingly. If you work here, full-time employees (excludes interns) expect to have access to the benefits below:

• Competitive compensation packages

• Medical, dental and vision benefits for employees and their dependents

• Paid Vacation

• 401(k) and pre-tax health insurance, dependent care, and commuter benefits (FSA)

Kairos Power is committed to building a diverse workforce that reflects the communities where we do business. Kairos Power is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. We actively welcome people of different experiences, abilities, and perspectives.

jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Data & Analytics
jobs.description:
About Us

Greenbrook Medical is building the new standard in primary care.

We deliver high-touch, relationship-based care through neighborhood clinics, grounded in a simple belief: every senior deserves the kind of care we would want for our own families. Our model prioritizes time with patients, strong care coordination, and a personalized approach that improves outcomes while lowering total cost of care.

We take full accountability for patient outcomes and overall cost of care, aligning clinical excellence with disciplined execution. That commitment shows up in our results, including a patient Net Promoter Score of 90, compared to 32 for typical healthcare organizations.

Rooted in Tampa Bay and partnered with Tampa General Hospital, we are entering an exciting phase of growth. Backed by strong unit economics, experienced operators, and a proven playbook, we are looking for builders and operators who want to help scale a healthcare platform designed to deliver better care, better coordination, and better outcomes for seniors.

About The Role

We're hiring our first dedicated data person. This person will build on our existing data platform, harden it to ensure consistent performance and build upon our metric library to ensure that our operators can monitor performance across all of our levers.

Success in this role means end to end ownership, from data platform to metric delivery and visualization in dashboarding tools

As Data and Analytics Engineer, you own four things:

• The analytics layer: the dbt models and business logic that turn raw data into something usable, and the metric definitions underneath them

• Reporting and BI: the reporting layer the whole business reads from

• Our production systems: you take ownership of systems as they come in-house from our engineering partner, harden them, and keep making them better, with accountability for uptime & system integrity

• The partnership with our engineering team: you are the internal counterpart who knows both the business and the systems well enough to resolve most issues directly

This is a build-and-own role. Our engineering partner stands up a new capability; you take it on once it is live, harden it, and keep improving it. You work as their peer rather than their coordinator. You also partner closely with the pop health team (who owns our value drivers) in defining metrics and deciding together what the business needs to see. You report to the VP of Growth and Population Health.

Location: New York City strongly preferred (Hybrid). Open to exceptional remote candidates.

What You'll Do

Own the Analytics Layer

• Build and maintain the dbt models and business logic our metrics and workflows depend on. Work within Google Cloud to iterate on our business logic and transformation infrastructure

• Ensure consistency in definitions across all surfaces at Greenbrook

• Work with the performance managers on what needs measuring and what good looks like in their areas

Take Ownership of What's in Production

• Take on systems as they move from our engineering partner into steady state, and keep them healthy

• Be accountable for uptime & system integrity – catch ingestion and pipeline issues or logic bugs and resolve them within our SLAs. Develop monitoring and uptime reporting.

• Ensure a performant system. Optimize workloads and runtime

• Keep improving what you take on rather than only maintaining it

Partner Across the Business

• Be the counterpart our engineering partner can hand production work to, resolving what you can and escalating what needs them

• Build dashboards to support organizational decisionmaking

• Work closely with the business – sit in the operating meetings where the data gets used, so you know what decisions it feeds

What Success Looks Like

• Data Trust: the business trusts the numbers, and you are ahead of issues rather than behind them

• Reliability: systems transitioned to you stay healthy, and when they break they get fixed quickly

• Coverage: the metrics our drivers depend on have a certified definition and a single source of truth

• Delivery: the work you committed to for the quarter shipped

• Metrics you'll own: delivery against committed quarterly work, and counterpart satisfaction among the performance managers and the Head of Population Health

About You

You bring:

• Fluency in dbt and Python

• Hands on experience with Health care datasets and interoperability frameworks which our business run on, including a deep understanding of claims, eligibility, EHR data, and frameworks such as FHIR and HL7

• A solid grasp of business fundamentals, enough to partner with business and clinical managers on defining metrics rather than only building to spec

• Experience owning production systems, including being the person who responds when something breaks

• Bachelor's degree required

• A mindset grounded in our core values of Heart, Excellence, Accountability, Resilience, and Teamwork

You'll stand out if you:

• Want to own a system deeply: you would rather take something into production, harden it, and keep improving it than move on to the next greenfield build

• Get to root cause: you find out why a number is wrong rather than patching the symptom

• Are AI-native: you live in modern AI tools to support your work

• Communicate with clarity: you are comfortable explaining complex data to business users and communicate proactively

• Own the outcome: high bias for action, follow through on commitments, and close loops without needing to be chased

Why You'll Love Working Here

Make An Impact Every Day

Be part of a mission-driven team transforming primary care for seniors. Your work directly supports better outcomes, better coordination, and better experiences for some of the most vulnerable patients in healthcare.

Work That Actually Matters

We're not a volume-driven system, we're accountable for outcomes. That means your work directly contributes to quality care, patient satisfaction, and meaningful improvements in how healthcare is delivered.

Build And Grow With Us

We're building more than a company, we're building careers. As we expand, you'll have opportunities to grow your skills and take on new challenges.

Strong, Transparent Compensation & Benefits

• $170,000 annually, based on experience and qualifications

• Generous annual performance bonus

• Health, dental, and vision insurance

• Paid time off

• 401(k) with company match

Our Selection Process

Application → Initial interview → Skills/experience interview → Values interview → Case Study and Case Study Interview → References

Equal Employment Opportunity and Commitment to Diversity

At Greenbrook Medical, we believe the only way we accomplish our mission is by building the best team in healthcare. We do this through a culture of respect and belonging, ensuring our teammates feel cared for first and foremost.

We will extend equal employment opportunity to all applicants without regard to age, race, ethnicity, sex, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, socioeconomic background, disability status, military affiliation, pregnancy or any other status protected under federal, state and local laws. We encourage all who share our mission to apply. Greenbrook Medical will provide reasonable accommodations during the recruitment process. If you need additional accommodations or assistance, do not hesitate to contact our People team at recruiting@greenbrookmedical.com.

The Security and Risk Engineering organization builds scalable, AI-powered security solutions that reduce risk and protect ServiceNow and its customers. We value AI-first thinking, clean architecture, intuitive experiences, and a culture of continuous learning.

This is a zero-to-one incubation. We’re building a new class of exposure analysis that ranks security work by exploitability—where an attacker could realistically get in—rather than raw severity. The architecture is evolving, and this role helps define what good looks like.

The role

As a Staff ML Engineer, you own a major subsystem of a novel exploitability engine end to end—for example the probability core, the exposure graph and entity-resolution layer, or the calibration and validation loop. You make the design calls within your area and drive them to production.

What you’ll own

• A major subsystem end-to-end—the probability core, the exposure graph and entity resolution, or the calibration and validation loop—including its design, delivery, and quality.
• The design decisions within your subsystem, and how it interfaces with the rest of the engine.
• The metrics that prove your subsystem works—entity-resolution accuracy, calibration quality, or path-ranking precision—owned as first-class targets.
• Technical direction for the engineers working in your area.

What you’ll do

• Take a major, ambiguous subsystem from design through production at scale.
• Drive design and code reviews in your area, and raise the engineering bar around you.
• Mentor engineers and lead a workstream through influence.
• Partner with product, security R&D, and SecOps to turn customer problems into subsystem design.

• A track record of owning a significant system or subsystem end-to-end in production.
• Hands-on depth in agentic and LLM systems and/or probabilistic or ML-driven scoring—graph modeling, calibration, search and optimization.

About the team

The Security and Risk Engineering organization builds scalable, AI-powered security solutions that reduce risk and protect ServiceNow and its customers. We value AI-first thinking, clean architecture, intuitive experiences, and a culture of continuous learning.

This is a zero-to-one incubation. We’re building a new class of exposure analysis that ranks security work by exploitability—where an attacker could realistically get in—rather than raw severity. The architecture is evolving, and this role helps define what good looks like.

As a Senior Staff Engineer, you own the architecture of an security harness with novel exploitability engine end to end, and you’re accountable for the decisions that shape everything downstream. You set technical direction, make the hard calls defensible, and multiply the engineers around you.

What you’ll own

• The end-to-end architecture of the exploitability engine—from evidence ingestion and entity resolution, through the attack-path probability core and choke-point ranking, to the validation loop that keeps predictions honest.
• The decisions that cascade through the system: calibrated probability versus ordinal rank, identity as a first-class graph edge, assume-breach seeding, and how the most critical assets are defined. These are model-shaping calls, not implementation details.
• The probabilistic ranking core: edge-traversal probability, guided path search with hop and likelihood limits, correlated-control-failure modeling, and honest uncertainty bands.
• The calibration and validation loop—canaries, purple-team and incident replay, calibration measured by zone and vector—that turns modeled weights into evidence rather than opinion.
• Make-or-break metrics as first-class engineering targets, starting with entity-resolution accuracy and calibration quality.

jobs.title: Staff Industrial Designer
jobs.description:
WHAT TO EXPECT

Heron Power Electronics is a company building cutting-edge power electronics products for the 21st-century grid. We aim to debottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and less costly hardware solutions, accelerating the sustainable electrification of everything.

Our first goal is to build better converters to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads like datacenters to the grid. Heron Power's leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products.

We believe great design is an important part of building great technology. Our products are physical machines, digital interfaces, tools, environments, documentation, and a brand—and the experience of Heron is shaped by all of them.

We understand that no one individual knows everything. We learn together, build together, and solve difficult problems from first principles. You can expect to work in a fast-moving, deeply technical environment where designers work directly with engineers, operators, customers, and leadership to turn complex technology into products and experiences that are clear, useful, thoughtful, and distinctly Heron.




JOB OVERVIEW

We are looking for a Staff Industrial Designer to help shape the products, experiences, and visual language of Heron Power Electronics.

This is a broad design role with industrial design at its center, spanning physical product design, product UX, visual communication, and brand. You might spend one project developing the form, architecture, interfaces, and details of a new power electronics product; another improving how an operator interacts with a product; and another creating the creating graphics, infographics, environmental elements, or documentation that make complex ideas clear.

You will work closely with the Head of Design and leadership across mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, manufacturing, software, commercial, and more. You'll move fluidly between defining a problem, exploring concepts, prototyping solutions, developing production-ready designs, and working with partners to bring them into the world.

As a Staff-level designer, you will be expected to operate with a high degree of autonomy, take ownership of ambiguous design problems, establish a strong point of view, move quickly from thinking to making, and help raise the quality and coherence of design across Heron.




HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE

 - Drive industrial design efforts across Heron's power electronics products, from early architecture and concept development through detailed design and production.

 - Work directly with mechanical, electrical, thermal, manufacturing, and systems engineers to understand technical constraints and turn them into thoughtful product solutions.

 - Explore product architecture, proportion, form, materials, finishes, interfaces, serviceability, manufacturing processes, and details.

 - Build quickly and think through making—using sketches, CAD, physical prototypes, renderings, mockups, animations, and whatever tools best address the question at hand.

 - Help define how people physically interact with Heron products, including installation, operation, service, access, controls, labeling, status communication, and safety.

 - Contribute to digital product UX where physical and digital experiences intersect, working with software teams to make complex systems understandable and intuitive.

 - Develop clear visual communication for complex technical ideas through diagrams, information graphics, presentations, product graphics, documentation, and other storytelling tools.

 - Extend and evolve Heron's visual identity across products, spaces, digital experiences, events, and communications.

 - Establish design systems, principles, and patterns that create consistency across an expanding family of Heron products and touchpoints.

 - Advocate for the user while balancing engineering performance, manufacturing, cost, reliability, safety, serviceability, and business requirements.

 - Raise the design bar across the company through strong craft, thoughtful critique, clear communication, and a willingness to get into the details and go the extra mile.
   
   


WHAT YOU WILL BRING

We're looking for an Industrial Designer with deep industrial design capability and unusually broad range.

You do not need to be equally specialized in every design discipline. We care more about excellent design judgment, strong execution, curiosity, and the ability to move confidently across different kinds of problems.




MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS

 - Significant professional experience designing and shipping physical products, with a portfolio demonstrating exceptional industrial design thinking and craft, strong taste, breadth across disciplines, and the ability to carry ideas from early exploration through polished execution.

 - Strong industrial design fundamentals, including form development, proportion, product architecture, CMF, ergonomics, manufacturing processes, and design detailing.

 - Strong 3D skills and experience developing concepts through CAD, rendering, prototyping, and physical models.

 - Heart. We are rebuilding the American grid. Solving extremely difficult and urgent problems. Laying the foundation for highly intelligent power infrastructure that can enable abundant, efficient, sustainable energy. This is a BFD. It should move you.

 - Experience collaborating closely with engineering teams and working within real technical, manufacturing, cost, and schedule constraints.

 - Strong graphic and visual communication skills, including layout, composition, typography, information hierarchy, diagrams, and presentation design.

 - Ability to take complex technical information and make it understandable through design.

 - Experience thinking about products as complete experiences—not just objects—including physical interaction, interfaces, installation, service, communication, and environment.

 - Ability to independently frame ambiguous problems, develop a point of view, communicate design rationale, and drive work forward with limited direction.

 - Low ego, high curiosity, strong internal drive, and sincere enthusiasm for collaborating with people from disciplines very different from your own.


NICE-TO-HAVES

jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Design Engineer - Structures & Systems
jobs.description:
Embark on a journey with QDSS at the forefront of technological innovation as we seek talented Engineers to shape the future of cutting-edge projects and contribute to a culture of excellence and creativity.  What we do matters.

Quest Defense Systems & Solutions is seeking an experienced Mechanical Design Engineer to lead the integration of aircraft structures and systems across the product lifecycle. This position will serve as a technical focal point for design architecture, interfaces, manufacturing integration, certification, and engineering change management.

• Location: Remote; Eastern or Central time zone preferred

• Preferred Proximity: Cincinnati, Ohio, or Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas

• Travel: Less than 25%

• Citizenship Requirement: Must qualify as a U.S. Person

• Security Clearance: Not required at the time of hire; ability to obtain a clearance in the future is preferred

What You Will Do:

• Lead conceptual layouts and integration solutions for aircraft structures and systems.

• Design primary and secondary structures, systems installations, and antenna installations for advanced connectivity systems.

• Define system architecture, interfaces, installation requirements, and Interface Control Drawings.

• Prepare structural and systems layouts, installation drawings, and detailed engineering drawings.

• Perform trade studies to optimize weight, cost, performance, and manufacturability.

• Develop and process Program Change Requests and manage modifications through configuration control.

• Evaluate the technical, cost, schedule, risk, and profitability impacts of proposed changes.

• Coordinate technical integration across Stress, Systems, Interiors, Aerodynamics, Mass Properties, Manufacturing, Quality, and Certification.

• Lead technical meetings with customers and suppliers and ensure the delivery of quality engineering documentation.

• Chair or support design reviews, risk assessments, and program milestone gates.

• Support manufacturing, production, and shop-floor issue resolution.

• Apply Design for Manufacturing and Design for Assembly principles.

• Support verification, validation, testing, qualification, and certification activities.

• Maintain accurate product lifecycle management and configuration data.

• Provide technical guidance and mentorship to other engineers.

Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline.

• At least 5 years of aerospace engineering experience involving aircraft structures or systems integration.

• Experience designing primary and secondary airframe structures and systems installations.

• Proficiency with CATIA V5 or Siemens NX.

• Experience developing layouts, installation drawings, interface drawings, and detailed designs.

• Knowledge of materials and processes, GD&T, aerospace design standards, and preliminary sizing.

• Understanding of aircraft systems, structural interfaces, manufacturing processes, and industrialization.

• Knowledge of CAR, FAR, or CS certification requirements and compliance processes.

• Experience with configuration management and PLM systems such as ENOVIA or Teamcenter.

• Strong technical leadership, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.

• Must qualify as a U.S. Person under applicable export-control regulations.

Desired Qualifications:

• Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline.

• At least 15 years of relevant aerospace engineering experience.

• Experience with antenna or aircraft connectivity-system installations.

• Knowledge of aircraft interiors integration and in-service maintenance constraints.

• French-language proficiency.

• Ability to obtain a U.S. security clearance in the future.

• Experience in the adoption and/or integration of emerging technologies (e.g., generative AI, automation platforms, digital assistants) into day-to-day operations for continuous improvement.

The QDSS Advantage:

At QDSS, our advantage is purpose-driven work, collaborative teams, and complex challenges that push boundaries and build lasting impact. You’ll grow your career while contributing to mission-critical programs that demand excellence and shape the future.

What You’ll Find Here

• Work That Matters – Next-generation, safety- and mission-critical projects where your contributions have real-world impact.

• Growth That’s Supported – Competitive compensation, employer-matched 401(k), certification assistance, and clear opportunities for advancement.

• A Culture That Works – A flexible, collaborative, and people-first environment where teamwork, innovation, and balance are valued.

Benefits Include

• Competitive pay, comprehensive medical/dental/life and disability coverage, 401(k) with employer match, professional development support, and a flexible, friendly workplace.

Full compensation package is based on candidate experience and certifications

Pay Ranges

$130,000—$145,000 USD

At Quest Defense Systems and Solutions, we don’t just build technology — we engineer the future. From next-generation aerospace solutions to cutting-edge defense systems, we tackle the toughest, mission-critical challenges that keep people safe and push the boundaries of innovation. This is where problem-solvers, innovators, and visionary thinkers come together to shape the future. With over 25 years of aerospace and defense engineering expertise, our commitment to delivering high-quality, transformative solutions sets us apart — not just as an industry leader, but as a driving force for impactful change. Together, we’re not just leading the industry — we’re revolutionizing it.

Position Summary...

What you'll do...

Role summary:
The (USA) Supervisor, Security leads and oversees security associates by coordinating workloads, monitoring performance, and ensuring compliance with corporate policies and regulatory standards. This role involves managing emergency responses, maintaining safety protocols, and fostering strong partnerships with internal and external stakeholders. The supervisor supports continuous improvement of security programs and procedures while promoting a secure environment. By providing guidance, coaching, and operational oversight, this position contributes to safeguarding assets, ensuring regulatory adherence, and delivering a safe and efficient workplace aligned with Walmart’s values and business objectives.
About the team:
The Physical Security team at Walmart Campus is dedicated to maintaining a safe and secure environment through proactive emergency response and comprehensive security management. This team develops and enforces security protocols, conducts threat assessments, and ensures compliance with corporate and regulatory standards. Collaborating with internal partners and external agencies, they provide tactical responses to life safety events and support continuous improvements in security operations. The team upholds integrity and professionalism while protecting associates, assets, and facilities, fostering a secure workplace aligned with Walmart’s commitment to safety and operational excellence.
What you'll do:

• Supervise associates by assigning duties-coordinating workloads.
• Provide coaching, feedback, and support while reinforcing company policies and procedures.
• Assist with hiring, onboarding, and training of new and existing associates.
• Build and maintain relationships with internal and external partners to promote a safe work environment.
• Respond to emergencies and implement incident command protocols when necessary.
• Ensure compliance with regulatory and corporate requirements, addressing violations and corrective actions.
• Support the development and improvement of safety, security, and training programs.
• Investigate security incidents, assess threats, and assist with mitigation efforts.
• Manage security systems and respond to alarm activations to protect people and assets.
• Foster a culture of integrity, respect, accountability, and continuous improvement.

What you'll bring:

• Proven experience supervising teams, including assigning duties, monitoring performance, and providing constructive feedback.
• Strong knowledge of safety, security, and emergency response protocols, including life safety incident management.
• Ability to ensure compliance with regulatory and corporate policies such as OSHA, Sarbanes-Oxley, and fire codes.
• Skilled in developing and maintaining relationships with internal and external partners to promote a secure environment.
• Experience in coaching, training, and onboarding associates to support operational excellence.
• Demonstrated integrity, accountability, and commitment to ethical standards and company values.
• Effective communication and collaboration skills to build trust and achieve business objectives.

jobs.title: Sr. Software Development Engineer, Inference Team - AWS Neuron
jobs.description:
AWS Neuron is the complete software stack for AWS Inferentia and Trainium, AWS purpose-built accelerators for cloud-scale machine learning. This senior software engineering role is part of the Machine Learning Inference Applications team and focuses on delivering high-performance model inference solutions for customer workloads running on Inferentia- and Trainium-powered instances.

The engineer will lead the development of core serving technologies within open-source frameworks (such as vLLM and SGLang) to enable customers to serve large-scale inference efficiently on AWS Neuron. The engineer will also drive excellence in inference framework optimization and engineering best practices.

The engineer will work closely with model development engineers, performance engineers, compiler engineers, and runtime engineers to ensure end-to-end model performance and deliver production-ready accuracy, scalability, and efficiency across a broad range of models and customer use cases.

Key job responsibilities
The engineer will lead the customization and optimization of open-source inference frameworks (vLLM, SGLang) on AWS Neuron—including core framework logic such as scheduling and model execution—applying state-of-the-art techniques in kernel development, parallel computation, distributed KV cache, speculative decoding, and systems engineering to deliver best-in-class LLM serving performance.

The engineer will also influence the team's technical roadmap by evaluating emerging inference research and translating it into production-ready features, and raise the bar through design leadership and mentorship. This role requires close collaboration across model development, compiler, runtime, and performance engineering teams.

About the team
Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship. Our senior members enjoy one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects that help our team members develop your engineering expertise so you feel empowered to take on more complex tasks in the future.

Basic qualifications:
- 5+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 5+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience
- 5+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 5+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team
- Fundamentals of Machine learning models, their architecture, training and inference lifecycles along with work experience on some optimizations for improving the model performance.

Preferred qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
- Hands-on experience with PyTorch or JAX, preferably involving developing and deploying LLMs in production on GPUs, AWS Neuron, TPUs, or other AI accelerator hardware
- Experience extending or contributing to inference frameworks such as vLLM or SGLang
- Kernel development experience (e.g., CUDA, Triton)

Startups are the enterprises of the future. These young companies are founded by ambitious people who have a desire to build something meaningful and to challenge the status quo. To address underserved customers or to challenge incumbents. They usually operate in an environment of scarcity: whether that’s capital, engineering resource, or experience. This is where you come in.

The AWS Startup Solutions Architecture team is dedicated to working with these early stage startup companies as they build their businesses. We’re here to make sure that they can deploy the best, most scalable, and most secure architectures possible – and that they spend as little time and money as possible doing so.

We are looking for technical builders who love the idea of working with early stage startups to help them as they grow. In this role, you’ll work directly with a variety of interesting customers and help them make the best (and sometimes the most pragmatic) technical decisions along the way. You’ll have a chance to build enduring relationships with these companies and establish yourself as a trusted advisor.

As well as spending time working directly with customers, you’ll also get time to “sharpen the saw” and keep your skills fresh. We have more than 200 services across a range of different categories and it’s important that we can help startups take advantages of the right ones. You’ll also play an important role as an advocate with our product teams to make sure we are building the right products for the startups you work with.

For the customers you don’t get to work with on a 1:1 basis, you’ll get the chance to share your knowledge more broadly by working on technical content and presenting at events.

Analytica is seeking a Senior Graph Database Developer to support a highly complex critical federal program requiring advanced graph-based data engineering and analytics capabilities. The ideal candidate will lead the design, development, and optimization of graph data models and associated ETL pipelines, supporting large-scale structured and unstructured datasets. This role requires deep expertise in graph database technologies, data modeling, and ETL processes, as well as the ability to collaborate across technical and stakeholder teams.

Analytica has been recognized by Inc. Magazine as the fastest-growing private US small business.  We work with U.S. government customers in health, civilian, and national security missions.  As a core member you’ll work with a diverse team of professionals to solve matters, architect nuisances, and come up with alternatives.  We offer competitive compensation with opportunities for bonuses, employer paid health care, training and development funds, and 401k match.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead graph database development and ETL processes on large-scale structured and unstructured datasets.
• Design, implement, and maintain graph data models, ensuring alignment with ontological references and business requirements.
• Develop and maintain data structures, schemas, indexes, and relationships to optimize performance, scalability, and analytical use cases.
• Identify and document entity relationships, referential integrity constraints, and key structures, including analysis of tradeoffs between alternative graph and hybrid schemas.
• Collaborate with database administrators, data engineers, and stakeholder teams to validate data accuracy, formatting, and reliability.
• Document graph models, ETL processes, and scripts consistent with industry best practices and government guidelines.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
• 7+ years of experience supporting enterprise database environments.
• 4+ years of Cypher experience including data modeling and query optimization.
• Strong experience designing and implementing ETL processes for large-scale data environments.
• Proficiency in SQL and data modeling, including schema design and performance optimization.
• Experience supporting federal financial, compliance, regulatory, or tax administration systems is highly preferred

jobs.description:
• You will manage a portfolio of 25 - 30+ clients, typically CISOs and Leaders of Cybersecurity, from global Fortune 1000 BFSI (Banking Financial Services, Insurance) organizations and large high-tech industries
• As their Executive Partner, you will be delivering value through regular briefings, a mix of on-site and virtual workshops, roundtables, webinars and by attending relevant Gartner events, etc.
• As someone who has previously been in their shoes before (or someone who has equivalent experience), you will use your knowledge and expertise, along with additional Gartner resources and research, to coach and mentor your clients on critical initiatives and obstacles for today and tomorrow specifically within the Security Risk Management space
• Collaboration is key. You will work closely with several internal Gartner teams to ensure value is delivered. These can include Sales teams, Analysts, Client Managers, and your peers across other domains
• This role is a client-facing position that requires a high level of Executive presence, adaptability and ability to build trust and deliver value. In addition, this role requires communication, diplomacy, coaching and presentation skills.
• Responsible for member retention and for contributing toward growth in the region through direct support of Gartner Sales in prospect cultivation, account plan development and value demonstration activities
• This is a predominantly a home-based role, where you will operate as an individual contributor managing your own calendar and other administrative tasks; you will be delivering value to your client portfolio virtually with approximately 25% onsite support.

We’d love to talk to you if you have:

• Bachelor's degree required. 15+ years of experience in executive security leadership roles, including CISO, Security Practice Leader, or equivalent, preferably within BFSI organizations.Proven experience leading and scaling enterprise security programs, operations, teams, and capabilities.Experience in executive-level consulting, sales, or client-facing leadership roles.Strong expertise in security strategy, risk management, and aligning cybersecurity initiatives to business objectives.Hands-on experience with modern security technologies and practices, including SIEM, IAM, threat and vulnerability management, endpoint, network and cloud security, application/product security, and AI security.Demonstrated success establishing security governance, metrics, board-level reporting, and vendor management programs.Ability to articulate and demonstrate the business value of cybersecurity to executive and board audiences.Prior consulting experience with a large consulting firm preferred but not required.

Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

About the role:

Gartner Analysts are industry thought leaders who create must-have insights, market predictions and best practices for a broad range of world-leading organizations. A Senior Director serves as a leader within Gartner’s Business and Technology Insights (BTI) group, establishing oneself as a credible voice within their designated market at local, regional and global levels. Utilizing exceptional research and analytical skills, a Senior Director plays a significant role in producing pragmatic and provocative insights which Gartner clients consume and apply to propel their business toward key objectives. They are a trusted source of advice for clients, reinforcing Gartner’s value every day by engaging them via in-person meetings, virtual meetings, sales support visits and Gartner conferences to discuss complex client challenges and offer appropriate recommendations.

What you will do:

● Create innovative, thought provoking, and highly leveraged “must-have insights” content

● Develop new insights and ideas through thought leadership and offer compelling, actionable approaches to client's needs and requests that accelerate the client's ability to act

● Develop in-depth analysis to identify the root cause of a client’s barriers or overall needs and reframe thinking to drive strategy forward

● Demonstrate thought leadership in establishing Insights positions across a team of analysts

● Bring provocative, independent insights to Gartner leaders that can evolve the course of a research agenda

● Research, analyze and predict market trends and shifts to provide clients and vendors with actionable insights

● Provide clients and prospects with actionable advice aligned to their designated content area via virtual or face-to-face interactions

● Create and deliver high value presentation materials on and off stage for Gartner events, industry and professional association conferences, and client briefings

● Support BTI and Sales: Provide sales support serving as voice of the market to help Insights teams create content and to drive engagement with clients to make progress against their critical priorities to grow their business

● Provide high quality and timely content peer review

● Build credibility as an industry expert to represent Gartner insights, methodology and strategy

● Actively participate in innovation, ideation, and research discussions and collaborate effectively with peers in the Insights community

● Identify research process improvements or develop new processes that help the team and BTI provide excellent service delivery

● Be a mentor and a coach by supporting more junior team members

● Be client-centric while actively seeking to help clients engage regularly and often with Gartner insights and interactions

What you will need:

● Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; Graduate degree preferred

● 12+ years of relevant field or industry experience

● Demonstrate experience communicating the value and ROI of AI investments to executives or senior leaders

● Experience/knowledge of translating AI capabilities to supply chain outcomes

● Experience/knowledge of assessing risk of AI in supply chain strategies

● Experience/knowledge of governing supply chain AI solutions

● Demonstrate success communicating the financial ROI and strategic value of AI investments to C-suite leaders

● Demonstrate executive presence; can immediately establish credibility with executives and additional stakeholders

● Strong organizational skills; ability to work under tight deadlines and produce high quality deliverables

● Demonstrate excellence in research and writing ability

● Strong written and verbal proficiency, analytical and presentation skills; ability to engage clients and respond effectively to questions

● Proficient in analyzing and synthesizing data; can effectively apply patterns and frameworks while drawing and defending conclusions to client challenges

● Strong communication skills - able to explain complex concepts concisely and simply

● Subject matter expertise; comfortable presenting at large and small-scale speaking engagements

● Strong business and financial acumen

● Deep knowledge of the global and competitive landscape within subject area as well as the interplay in that market

● Ability to work independently, while also being intrinsically motivated to collaborate across teams and support the workflow of others, in a multicultural global team

● Learning agile and adept with navigating highly matrixed environments

● Ability to represent Gartner's research methodology and strategies effectively at all levels

● Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% (where applicable)

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

Job Description

Assistente de Reparos:

O Assistente de Reparos com foco na área de metalização, será responsável por apoiar na execução de processos relacionados à aplicação de revestimentos metálicos em peças aeronáuticas. As atividades incluem preparação de superfícies, mascaramento de áreas específicas, leitura e interpretação de desenhos técnicos, além de garantir a qualidade e precisão dos processos realizados sempre sob supervisão de profissionais mais experientes. O profissional trabalhará em conformidade com os protocolos de segurança e padrões de qualidade estabelecidos.

Responsabilidades:

Realizar atividades de mascaramento para proteção de áreas específicas durante o processo de metalização.

Preparar superfícies para aplicação de revestimentos metálicos, garantindo a aderência e qualidade do processo.

Interpretar desenhos técnicos para execução precisa das tarefas.

Manusear e organizar ferramentas e equipamentos utilizados no processo de metalização.

Garantir a limpeza e conservação de equipamentos e ferramentas.

Checar todos os parâmetros do processo para assegurar a qualidade de acordo com os documentos aplicáveis.

Trabalhar em conformidade com os protocolos de segurança e padrões de qualidade.

Qualificações Requeridas:

Ensino médio completo.

Curso técnico em mecânica industrial ou áreas correlatas.

Conhecimento ou curso de programação CNC (FANUC será considerado um diferencial).

Experiência prévia em processos de metalização ou áreas relacionadas será um diferencial.

Leitura e interpretação de desenhos técnicos.

Características Desejadas:

Proatividade e atitude positiva.

Bom relacionamento interpessoal e capacidade de trabalhar em equipe.

Senso de organização e atenção aos detalhes.

Facilidade de comunicação.

Disponibilidade para trabalhar de segunda a sábado, em turnos (2º e 3º turno) e regime 4x4.

Diferenciais:

Experiência em processos de mascaramento para metalização.

Conhecimento em programação CNC (Fanuc).

Participação no programa Jovem Aprendiz da GE Celma

jobs.description:
Business Introduction
GSK remains committed to achieving bold commercial ambitions for the future. By 2031, we aim to deliver £40 billion in annual sales, leveraging our existing strong performance momentum to significantly increase our positive impact on the health of billions of patients globally. Our Ahead Together strategy is centred on early intervention to prevent and alter the course of disease, thereby protecting people and supporting healthcare systems.
Our diverse portfolio consists of vaccines, specialty medicines, and general medicines.
Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges.

Position Summary

As a Director, Market Access Account Integration it will be critical to execute our Market Access strategy and build relationships with key stakeholders in the healthcare ecosystem. This role is responsible for managing business relationships with the largest influencers within the ecosystem including regional payers, mid-size PBMs, specialty provider groups, large employers, and coalitions. These customers are critical influencers of patient access and future innovation.

In this role, YOU will have the opportunity to lead critical activities to progress YOUR career. The responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:

• Develop and execute strategic account plans for regional payers, Specialty contract customers (MCOs, infusion and infusion management groups), large employers, and coalitions. Looking across customers and markets impacted by the ecosystem.
• Coordinate the account management model and identify opportunities for enterprise-level engagement to ensure access and drive top-down demand.
• Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, including payers, mid-size PBMs, provider customer and non-retail contract accounts, including economic decision makers within clinic systems, infusion management organizations, etc.
• Own and manage the strategic plan for account performance, including monitoring contract compliance and performance.
• Owns key market segmentation and customer prioritization holistically representing market access strategies, health care economics, regional and state policies.
• Responsible for contract management of payers and mid sized PBMs (RFPs, contract renewals, deal creation)
• Works collaboratively across the business units to represent the full GSK portfolio and Specialty account management.
• Provide insights and recommendations to optimize pricing, payer and provider contracting, including above brand initiatives.
• Monitor and analyze market trends, payer behaviors, and competitive activities to inform strategy.
• Collaborate with Market Access Contracting Strategy and Integrated Business Commercialization Team leads to ensure Gross-to-Net targets are met across specialty brands by sharing and evaluating the impact of business decisions and engaging in tradeoff decisions
• Build and cultivate influential relationships with key influencers including at the C-Suite level as it pertains to GSK portfolio.
• Establish alignment across internal GSK stakeholders to enable optimal coordination of customer engagement so the full value of GSK’s offerings can be realized.

Why You?

Basic qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree - BA/BS required.

• 7 + years of demonstrated experience in market access and account management and / or leadership experience.
• Valid driver’s license
• Open to 50-60% travel

Preferred Qualifications:

If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus:

• MBA and/or advanced clinical/science degree or equivalent Financial acumen and strong understanding of gross profit, erosion, ASP, Net Cost Recovery, and pricing impact preferred.
• Minimum of 3 years in regional payers and / or large contracted customers, mid-size PBMs, and coalitions
• Experience working in highly matrixed environment and influencing across multiple stakeholder groups with an enterprise mindset.
• Demonstrated high learning agility and ability to adapt and pivot to continually changing product portfolio
• Initiative-taker excited to step in to achieve goals with a strong history of demonstrated performance
• Strong account selling skills and ability to grow business through strategic planning and execution
• Effective communication and strong presentation skills Ability to apply Compliance Policies and Procedures (CPP) in unstructured and fluid situations
• Strong understanding of market access strategies, healthcare economics and reimbursement models that influence the local ecosystem and access.

How to Apply
We welcome your interest. Please apply to share how your experience and values align with our mission. We look forward to learning about what you will bring to the team.

#LI-GSK

#GSKCommercial

Skills

Account Management, Cross-Functional Work, Data to Insights, Digital Fluency, Omnichannel, Scientific Literacy

Please visit  GSK US Benefits Summary  to learn more about the comprehensive benefits program GSK offers US employees.

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.
