jobs.title: Mechanical Systems Design Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:

Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures.




WHO WE ARE:

We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy.




WHO YOU ARE:

Astro Mechanica is seeking an experienced Mechanical Systems Design Engineer to join our growing team. The ideal candidate is someone who can take full ownership of hardware design from concept to production and has a deep understanding of their impact on surrounding systems. Technical challenges are resolved from first principles. Your work at Astro Mechanica will have a direct impact on the configuration and performance of the Astro Mechanica demonstrator aircraft.

In this role, your mission will be to shepherd novel airframe integration and component hardware from whiteboard design through analysis, qualification, vehicle integration, and aircraft flight.




WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Perform trade studies and first-order analyses to inform component design and system architecture decisions

 - Complete detailed component designs and drawings. Validate your designs with structural, thermal, and/or fluid analyses

 - Collaborate closely with propulsion, structures, avionics, controls, and manufacturing teams to ensure seamless component and system integration

 - Work with suppliers to specify, select, and qualify off-the-shelf and/or custom components

 - Develop and conduct hardware test plans and analyze data to verify requirements and performance metrics meet design intent

 - Provide hands-on support during prototyping, vehicle builds, ground testing, and flight test campaigns

 - Participate in technical reviews, generate clear documentation, and contribute to safety and hazard analyses




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field

 - 2–5+ years of experience designing, integrating, or testing fluid or mechanical systems 

 - Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes, precision measurement and GD&T

 - Proficiency in 3D CAD tools (NX, CATIA V5, SolidWorks, or similar) for routing, packaging, and component design

 - Solid understanding of mechanical system, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer fundamentals and analysis methods

 - Hands-on experience with hardware— fabrication, assembly, or testing

 - Takes initiative for continuous improvement (not just completing assigned tasks)

 - Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, evolving development environment




PERKS & BENEFITS:

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, including Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)

 - 401(k) program and transparent stock option plan

 - Self-managed and flexible time-off policy, including PTO, paid holidays, and sick time

 - Flexible work environment
   
   


ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role.

Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

What We Do

We’re on a mission to empower animal healthcare professionals with opportunities to earn more and achieve greater flexibility in their careers and personal lives.

Powered by groundbreaking technology, Roo has built the industry-leading veterinary staffing platform, connecting Veterinarians, Technicians, and Assistants with animal hospitals for relief work and hiring opportunities. Roo empowers the largest network of over 20,000 veterinary professionals to help more than 9,000 animal hospitals provide quality care to more pets.
Together, we’ve provided more than  3 million hours of healthcare, helping Veterinarians earn more than $200 million.

About the Role

Roo Veterinary is building the modern labor marketplace and operating system for veterinary care. We help hospitals reliably staff shifts and access great veterinary professionals, so care happens when it’s needed, without burning out teams.

We’re hiring a VP of Sales to lead our efforts at building a high-performing sales organization and enhancing the sales culture of the company. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a key member of the management team, you’ll be accountable for growth on both sides of the marketplace, activating new hospitals and new providers (veterinarians and technicians) and growing volume through deepening provider engagement with Account Management programs

Key Responsibilities

• Own the integrated revenue strategy tied to company goals and unit economics.

• Design the coverage/territory/segment model across the revenue org (roles, handoffs, specialization, capacity).

• Allocate headcount and budget by ROI and constraints, maintaining a healthy cost of sales as you grow. Rebalance quickly when necessary.

• Build the operating cadence that makes forecast accuracy and quota attainment the default.

• Scale repeatable GTM playbooks across segments while preserving segment nuance.

• Build an enablement engine (messaging, objection handling, discovery, onboarding, ongoing coaching).

• Implement QA loops (call scoring, pipeline hygiene, deal reviews) with a clear iteration rhythm.

• Build a high-bar leadership bench and org design that scales (spans/layers/specialization).

• Set hiring rubrics and enforce the bar; build a coaching culture and accountability.

• Set performance standards and upgrade talent decisively—without destroying morale (consistent calibration, early underperformance plans, fast hard calls, keep top talent energized and growing).

• Own org-level capacity planning that maximizes ROI; drive org-wide clarity on definitions and leading indicators.

• Own the GTM systems architecture (CRM + tooling) with disciplined build-vs-buy judgment.

• Drive thoughtful automation that removes toil, enforces standards, and comes with real adoption plans.

• Align Product, Marketing, Finance, and Data around top revenue bets; secure resourcing for priorities and resolve tradeoffs quickly. Ensure opportunities are framed in a shared metrics backbone across functions—principled, not political.

• Lead major org/process/comp transformations while maintaining performance—protect the quarter while upgrading the machine.

What You Bring

• Proven Sales Leadership: Marketplace sales experience (or B2B SMB & Mid-market - services with a quota-carrying motion.

• Executive Presence + Clarity: crisp communicator with board-ready narrative discipline; high-integrity, no-spin, credible variance explanations.

• Genius-Maker: known for developing strong team - hiring great talent, upgrading fairly and quickly, and building a coaching culture that lifts performance.

• Rigor: track record of building accurate forecasting, measured motions, clean pipelines and a systematic approach.

• Data + Unit Economics Orientation: comfortable tying decisions to metrics without losing the plot on growth.

• Cross-functional Leadership: strong partner to Product/Marketing/Finance/Data; you can resolve tradeoffs, earn trust, and drive alignment around shared metrics.

While we are a remote first company, if you are based in San Francisco this will be a hybrid role.

Core Values

Our Core Values are what shape us as an organization and we're looking for people who exhibit the same values in their professional life; Bias to Urgency, Drive Measurable Impact, Seek Understanding, Solve Customer Problems and Have Fun!

What to expect from working at Roo!

For permanent, full time employees, we offer:

What you'll do

As the engineering manager for Billing Collections, you’ll own the operational and technical direction of the platforms that help Stripe users collect revenue reliably. You’ll lead the team that builds flexible, intelligent collection experiences that improve payment success, support customers through changing circumstances, and help businesses reduce unpaid balances and accelerate cash flow. You’ll shape the team as it expands to support increasingly sophisticated business models and global payment needs while working backwards from internal and external customers.

Responsibilities

• Lead a team responsible for the core architecture needed to enable billing collection

• Own the technical strategy and roadmap for billing collection

• Drive operational excellence across billing infrastructure systems

• Hire and develop engineers as the team expands into new scope

• Partner with stakeholders across organizations to deliver billing solutions

• Work backwards from internal and external customer needs to define priorities and scope

• Define and uphold engineering standards across a team owning business-critical billing infrastructure

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• 4+ years of engineering management experience, directly managing and growing teams of 5+ engineers focused on building and shipping products at scale

• 8+ years of full-time software development experience

• Track record of leading engineering teams responsible for high-traffic, low-latency, and extensible systems

• Deep user empathy with a history of working backwards from internal and external customer needs

• Proven ability to drive rigorous decision-making and build strong partnerships across teams

• Ability to handle ambiguity, creatively solve complex challenges, and execute on competing high-impact priorities

• Demonstrated focus on system reliability, operational health, and incident response

Preferred qualifications

• Experience building and leading distributed teams across multiple locations and time zones

• Track record of delivering shared infrastructure across multiple business units

• Background in billing, metering, or large-scale distributed systems

• Experience with payment mandates, recurring payment authorization, or related payment infrastructure

jobs.title: Senior Financial Analyst, Supply Chain Finance - Manufacturing
jobs.description:
BUILT ON FLAVOR.  FUELED BY PEOPLE.

What’s it like to work at Kinder’s? Well, there’s a lot of snacking and geeking out over what we all cooked over the weekend. Beyond that, there’s also plenty of hard work. Because we don’t just like flavor, we’re obsessed with it.

With over 100 products sold nationwide, we’re now a top-five brand in multiple flavor categories at Costco, Walmart, Whole Foods, and more. We’re not your typical CPG company. Privately held and founder-led, we like to think of ourselves as a pirate ship in a sea of cruise ships. Our crew is adventurous and fearless. We chart our own course and chase big ideas to make food unforgettable.

As we expand globally and approach $1 billion in revenue, we need more smart-and-scrappy, flavor-obsessed people to come aboard. If you’re looking for a place where you can see the real impact of your work... this is it! Every day, you’ll be part of a journey to add flavor to millions of meals and lives.

About This Role:

At Kinder's, we're passionate about flavor, quality, and creating exceptional food experiences. As our company continues to grow, so does the scale and complexity of our supply chain across co-manufacturing, logistics, and an expanding SKU portfolio.

The Senior Financial Analyst, Supply Chain Finance - Manufacturing will provide analytical and financial support to the Co-Manufacturing organization. This role will develop the reporting, models, and insights needed to understand product cost drivers and improve manufacturing performance across Kinder's external production network.

Working closely with Co-Manufacturing, Supply Chain Finance, Operations, and Accounting, this analyst will evaluate conversion costs, yield, scrap, labor, overhead, capacity, and productivity. The role will investigate variances, maintain accurate forecasts, and turn detailed operating data into clear business implications and recommended actions.

This position is well suited for a highly analytical self-starter who enjoys working with large and imperfect data sets, solving ambiguous problems, and building repeatable tools in a growing organization.

Key Responsibilities Include:

Manufacturing Reporting & Analysis

• Prepare monthly and weekly reporting for co-manufacturing costs and operational performance, including cost per unit, conversion cost, yield, scrap, labor, overhead, capacity utilization, and plant efficiency.

• Analyze actual results versus budget, forecast, standard, and prior periods; identify root causes, quantify financial impacts, and communicate conclusions clearly.

• Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that connect manufacturing KPIs to COGS, gross margin, EBITDA, inventory, and cash flow.

• Reconcile operational, supplier, ERP, and financial data and resolve data quality issues with business partners.

• Support period-end close through accrual analysis, co-manufacturing cost validation, true-ups, and review of unusual transactions.

• Develop ad hoc analyses in response to business questions and deliver accurate, decision-focused outputs under tight timelines.

Planning, Costing & Decision Support

• Support the annual budget, rolling forecast, and long-range planning processes for co-manufacturing costs and related operational drivers.

• Maintain forecast models for conversion costs, productivity, yield, labor, overhead, capacity, and other manufacturing assumptions.

• Develop and maintain should-cost models for co-manufacturing toll estimates, supplier negotiations, and cost validation.

• Quantify manufacturing productivity and cost-reduction initiatives, track performance against commitments, and validate realized savings.

• Support business cases for capacity investments, make-versus-buy decisions, network changes, capital expenditures, and co-manufacturing alternatives.

• Provide financial support for new product introductions, reformulations, pack changes, and manufacturing transitions.

Business Partnership & Process Improvement

• Partner with Co-Manufacturing, Operations, Accounting, Procurement, R&D, and Finance to understand cost drivers and improve financial outcomes.

• Translate detailed manufacturing results into concise insights and recommendations for finance and non-finance audiences.

• Build repeatable models, reporting tools, and documentation that improve the accuracy, speed, and scalability of Manufacturing Finance processes.

• Identify control gaps, inconsistencies, and opportunities to improve cost visibility; propose and implement practical solutions.

• Manage multiple priorities independently, escalate material issues promptly, and follow analyses through to resolution.

Skills & Experience:

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field.

• 3+ years of progressive finance, accounting, analytics, manufacturing finance, operations finance, or FP&A experience.

• Strong understanding of COGS, standard costing, variance analysis, gross margin, inventory, and manufacturing cost drivers.

• Experience analyzing productivity, yield, scrap, labor, overhead, conversion costs, or capacity is strongly preferred.

• Experience in Consumer Packaged Goods, food, manufacturing, retail, or another inventory-intensive business is preferred.

• Advanced Excel / Google Sheets skills, including the ability to organize and analyze large data sets and build scalable financial models.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with close attention to detail, data integrity, and reconciliation.

• Ability to communicate complex analysis clearly and tailor conclusions for finance and non-finance audiences.

• Ability to work autonomously, manage competing deadlines, and make progress when processes or data are still evolving.

• Experience with BI tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or Looker is a plus.

• Experience with ERP and planning systems such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Anaplan, or comparable platforms is a plus.

Location and Travel:

The position will be based onsite in Walnut Creek, CA. We strongly believe in the power of culture and community and have a hybrid work structure with 4 days in the office on a weekly basis to encourage collaboration and personal connections that will allow us to better serve our customers and consumer and to have more fun. Fridays are flex days with employees having the opportunity to choose to be either in the office or to work from home based on what makes most sense for them.

Pay Transparency:

The expected starting salary range for this role is $115,000- $125,000 per year. The salary range posted for this role reflects the good-faith base pay range Kinder’s reasonably expects to offer at the time of posting and may vary based on the location of the role. Individual compensation within the posted range will be determined based on factors such as relevant education, experience, qualifications, skills, and business needs.

SEASONED FOR SUCCESS:

• No two days here are the same.

• We try to be good team members and good communicators, but we don’t live by hierarchy and structure – everyone is a difference maker here.

• We make a lot of decisions in the face of incomplete information – our team embraces ambiguity and tries to make good decisions fast rather than great decisions slow.

• We believe our job is to take smart risk, not to eliminate risk.

• We believe in growing our skills and becoming a better company with more managerial expertise, but we are an entrepreneurial company at heart.

• We aren’t trying to be average – we want to do exceptional things, and we are willing to work hard to achieve them.

BENEFITS THAT BRING MORE TO THE TABLE:

We offer a range of total rewards that may include paid time off, 401k, bonus / incentive eligibility, equity grants, competitive health benefits, and other family-friendly benefits, including parental leave. Kinder’s benefits vary based on eligibility and can be reviewed in more detail during the interview process.

OUR RECIPE FOR BALANCE:

We believe great culture starts with people. We’re a people-first company built on connection, collaboration, and balance. Most of our work happens in the office to spark creativity and community, but we also offer flexibility so team members have the autonomy to work outside the office when needed to support their work-life balance and personal commitments.

WHERE EVERY INGREDIENT MATTERS:

Kinder's is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, gender, citizenship, marital status, religion, age, disability, gender identity, results of genetic testing, veteran status, as well as any other legally-protected characteristic. If you have a disability under the Americans with Disabilities Act or similar law, and you need any accommodation during the application process or to perform these job requirements, please reach out to us at careers@kinders.com

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Search
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

We're building Anthropic's search platform team to create scalable, efficient search capabilities that power Claude's ability to access and retrieve information. In this role, you'll design and implement core search systems from the ground up.

Responsibilities:

• Work with a small, senior team of engineers and researchers to build Anthropic’s search platform from scratch

• Establish metrics and tooling to measure and improve search quality

• Enhance search algorithms and indexing mechanisms to boost search accuracy and efficiency

You may be a good fit if you:

• 5+ years building complex distributed systems in production

• Solid grasp of search fundamentals: indexing, retrieval, ranking

• Strong coding skills in Python, Go, Java, or similar languages

• Hands-on experience with high-volume data processing architectures

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$1—$2 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.description:
Provide advanced critical care and emergency medical support within a fast-paced international healthcare environment serving U.S. government personnel in Iraq. Working alongside physicians, nurses, and multidisciplinary emergency response teams, this Critical Care Paramedic role combines high-acuity patient care with rapid clinical assessment, advanced intervention, and collaborative care coordination across emergency response and inter-facility transport operations.

This position offers the opportunity to manage complex medical and trauma cases while practicing at an advanced clinical level in a highly collaborative operational setting.

Location: Iraq

Assignment Details: This is a full-time, fixed-term role of up to 12 months. Separate PRN opportunities are also available. Housing, meals, and project-related airfare are company-paid.

Key Responsibilities

• Deliver advanced life support and critical care interventions during emergency responses and inter-facility transports across a broad range of medical and traumatic presentations.
• Assess, stabilize, and manage critically ill or injured patients using advanced airway management, cardiac monitoring, medication administration, and resuscitative care techniques.
• Operate and interpret specialized critical care equipment including ventilators, infusion pumps, cardiac monitors, and 12-lead ECGs to support patient treatment and transport decisions.
• Collaborate closely with physicians, nurses, and healthcare teams to support continuity of care across emergency, inpatient, and outpatient clinical environments.
• Support operational readiness through accurate documentation, equipment management, supply oversight, and participation in ongoing training and clinical competency activities.

• Current unrestricted Paramedic license.
• Current CCP-C or FP-C certification required.
• Current BLS, ACLS, and advanced trauma certification (PHTLS, ITLS, TCCC, or equivalent).
• Recent high-acuity paramedic or critical care transport experience with advanced emergency response responsibilities.
• U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident with a valid passport

jobs.description:

jobs.title: Construction Systems Specialist
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Design & Construction team at Anduril delivers the factories, labs, offices, and secure spaces that enable our teams to design, build, and deploy advanced defense technology. Our projects span high-performance manufacturing facilities, mission-critical secure environments, and collaborative workspaces, giving our team exposure to a uniquely wide variety of technical and operational challenges. More than just delivering buildings, we are (literally) rebuilding the American defense industrial base. Our work directly accelerates how quickly critical technology moves from concept to production and into the hands of the warfighter.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Capital Operations team sits within the broader Design & Construction organization at Anduril. We are responsible for providing the critical support needed to bring our sites to life. We do so by creating, maintaining, and executing key operational process, analytics, and tools. All the while, we are collaborating with a variety of stakeholders involved in shaping the built environment needed to enable Anduril's mission (construction managers, architects, industrial engineers, real estate planners, finance analysts, and many more). But, first and foremost, we deeply listen to what our Division Leaders need. Whether it is autonomous submarines, robot fighter jets, or AR headsets, we stay close to our end users to ensure we're fueling their success.

This is the team's Construction Systems role. You'll be the true product owner of the software platforms that run our Design & Construction organization, starting with our new Project Management Information System (PMIS), standing up projects, evolving the platform's capabilities, managing its integrations, and training our entire Project Management team who live in it every day, with room to grow into other construction tools over time.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• PMIS Product Ownership:

• Act as the true product owner for our Project Management Information System — owning its configuration, roadmap, and day-to-day operation, and continuously evolving the platform as the team’s needs grow.

• Continued feature evolution: Configure and roll out new business processes and modules across the platform’s functional areas — portfolio and budget management, contracts and procurement, change orders, invoices and payment applications, document management and submittals, field management, and closeout.

• Own the backlog: Partner closely with project managers, construction managers, and project controls to understand pain points and translate them into prioritized system improvements.

• Project Setup & System Administration:

• Stand up individual projects in the system including initial data entry, project configuration, roles, and templates so teams can start working immediately.

• System administration: Own user provisioning, role-based access, libraries, report configuration, and data integrity across the portfolio.

• Data migration: Build and maintain data import templates and lead the collection, import, and validation of project data for new and in-flight projects.

• Integrations, Reporting & Data:

• Manage integrations between the PMIS and our ERP, Airtable, and other systems, ensuring financial and project data flow accurately and stay in sync.

• Partner on architecture: Work with Anduril Corporate Technology and other stakeholders to maintain, troubleshoot, and extend these integrations over time.

• Reporting & dashboards: Build and maintain the reports and dashboards that give project teams and executives a real-time, centralized view of budgets, commitments, risks, and status.

• Training & Adoption:

• Train all Anduril Project Managers and external Owner’s Reps on the system through both group sessions and 1:1 support, and drive adoption of the platform as the single source of truth.

• Documentation & support: Create and maintain training materials, standard operating procedures, and help resources; run helpdesk / office-hours sessions and refine materials based on user feedback.

• Primary point of contact for user questions, troubleshooting, and escalations.

• Implementation & Sustainment:

• Hands-on delivery: Play an active role in bringing the PMIS from build through go-live and into long-term sustainment — helping design business processes, configure the system, test workflows, and support pilot and full-team rollouts.

• Operating rhythm: Establish the ongoing cadence that keeps the platform reliable, secure, and continuously improving well after launch.

• Future Systems (Growth Over Time):

• Expand your remit beyond the PMIS to additional construction technology tools (such as scheduling software), applying the same product-owner discipline: evaluate, implement, integrate, and drive adoption across the portfolio.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Minimum of 6 years of experience implementing, administering, or owning enterprise project management, project controls, or construction management software (e.g., Oracle Unifier / Primavera, Procore, Kahua, e-Builder, or similar).

• Hands-on system configuration experience: you can independently build and modify business processes, workflows, forms, reports, and user permissions — not just operate a system that others configured.

• Experience managing software integrations with ERP or financial systems, and a working understanding of how data flows between platforms (Oracle Fusion experience is a strong plus).

• A product owner’s mindset: you gather requirements from non-technical users, prioritize a roadmap, and translate business needs into system capabilities.

• Strong training and communication skills: you can teach busy project and construction managers to adopt new tools through group and 1:1 sessions, and produce clear documentation.

• Comfort operating amid ambiguity and driving a platform from implementation through long-term sustainment.

• Willingness to travel up to 10% of the time (international travel included) for select trainings and systems configurations.

• Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience in construction, capital projects, or an Owner’s organization (Owner’s Representative, general contractor, or corporate real estate / construction).

• Experience with advanced manufacturing-related or mission-critical facility projects.

• Familiarity with construction financial processes: budgets, commitments, change orders, invoices / payment applications, and cost forecasting.

• Experience with reporting / BI tools and low-code data platforms (e.g., Airtable, Power BI).

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.

US Salary Range

$146,000—$194,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

jobs.title: Senior Accounting Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT BRINC:

At BRINC, we are building the technology that will define the future of emergency response. As a vertically integrated U.S. drone technology company, BRINC designs and manufactures unmanned aircraft systems, autonomous drone stations, command-and-control software, and advanced autonomy for public safety. Today, BRINC deploys Drone as First Responder (DFR) networks that dispatch drones directly to 911 calls, providing real-time aerial intelligence before ground units arrive and helping first responders make faster, safer decisions. BRINC serves more than 1,000 public safety customers across all 50 states, is the sole drone supplier to Motorola Solutions, and has raised more than $280 million from leading strategic and technology investors, including Motorola Solutions, Index Ventures, Sam Altman, Dylan Field, and others. BRINC is recruiting exceptional engineers to build the next generation of autonomous emergency-response technology, including flight-critical firmware and advanced pilot-assistance capabilities.




ABOUT THIS ROLE:

As the Senior Accounting Manager at BRINC, you will play a pivotal role in managing our financial operations and ensuring compliance with accounting standards. Reporting to the Head of Finance, you will own the day-to-day accounting function and work closely with others on the finance & operations team as well as other departments to maintain accurate financial records, analyze & report data, and contribute to strategic decision-making processes. You will own the preparation for our first audit.  This position offers a unique opportunity to join a startup in scale up mode and create accounting processes from the ground up.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Oversee day-to-day accounting operations, including general ledger entries, payroll processing, and revenue recognition, ensuring proper documentation of conclusions in accordance with ASC 606 for all subscription, hardware, and service arrangements.

 - Lead audit readiness and coordinate the company’s first financial statement audit, including preparation of work papers, schedules, and auditor requests.

 - Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in accordance with GAAP.

 - Manage the month-end and year-end close processes, including journal entries, accruals, and account reconciliations, ensuring timely and accurate reporting.

 - Oversee overall tax compliance, including federal, state, local, sales, and payroll taxes, and partner with external tax advisors to coordinate annual filings and other applicable requirements.

 - Drive process improvements and efficiency initiatives within the finance function.

 - Assist in budgeting and forecasting processes to support strategic planning efforts.

 - Support cross-functional teams on ad hoc projects and initiatives as needed.

 - Oversee inventory and cost accounting, including work in process, finished goods, and cost of goods sold.

 - Develop and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and internal controls appropriate for a high-growth organization.

 - Evaluate and implement scalable accounting systems and automation tools, including the company’s future ERP environment.




QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field; CPA certification preferred

 - 7+ years of progressive accounting experience

 - Experience working in a fast-paced startup environment, combined with hands-on knowledge of manufacturing operations

 - Strong knowledge of US GAAP and proficiency in financial reporting

 - Demonstrated experience managing an audit process, including selection of and interaction with external auditors

 - Hands-on experience implementing financial systems (AR/AP tools or an ERP) to streamline finance & accounting operations

 - Ability to leverage AI tools and automated workflows to optimize accounting operations, enhance variance analysis, and drive close/reporting efficiencies

 - Expert in accounting software (e.g., QuickBooks Online, NetSuite) and proficient with Microsoft Excel/Google Sheets

 - Proficient in SaaS subscription management/AR software

 - Excellent analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial data and communicate informed recommendations across multiple stakeholders

 - Detail-oriented with a commitment to accuracy and integrity in financial reporting
   
   


PREFERRED SKILLS:

 - Experience in people management/team mentorship
   
   


BRINC CULTURE VALUES:

 - Try the hard stuff

 - Be innovative - Invent the future

 - Move fast

 - Listen to end-users

 - Strive for excellence

 - Don’t build a dystopia

 - Be frugal

 - Save lives through technology
   
   

If you’re interested in this role and in joining BRINC, we hope you’ll apply. We’d love to review your application and get to know more about you!

jobs.title: Character Art Lead
jobs.description:
Summary

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Character Art Lead to lead our character art team and help define the visual quality and direction of our characters. As Character Art Lead, you will be responsible for setting artistic and technical standards, making strategic decisions that shape the character art pipeline and production process, and ensuring the team consistently delivers high-quality work that supports the creative vision of the game. You will partner closely with the Art Director, Production, Technical Art, Animation, and external development partners to establish priorities, solve complex challenges, and guide the team toward delivering exceptional character assets.

Core Responsibilities

• Lead, mentor, and provide clear artistic direction and feedback to the character art team, fostering a high-performing and collaborative environment.

• Partner with the Art Director to establish and maintain the visual language, quality bar, and artistic standards for characters.

• Make strategic decisions around character art workflows, pipelines, tools, and processes to improve quality, efficiency, and scalability.

• Establish priorities and help determine the appropriate allocation of character art resources across internal teams, outsourcing, and co-development partners.

• Work closely with Production and Directors to assess scope, prioritize work, identify risks, and make informed tradeoffs to keep character art production on track.

• Evaluate character art at key stages of development and provide actionable feedback to ensure assets meet the project's artistic and technical standards.

• Collaborate with Animation, Technical Art, and Engineering to establish character asset requirements and ensure characters are successfully integrated into the game.

• Define and maintain character art documentation, workflows, and best practices to support consistency, onboarding, and team development.

• Identify opportunities to improve the character art pipeline and proactively address production challenges before they impact the project.

• Stay current with evolving character art techniques, technology, and industry practices, and assess their potential value to the project.

Core Qualifications

• Proven experience setting artistic direction, establishing quality standards, and making strategic decisions for a character art team.

• Experience creating character pipelines from the ground up.

• Proven experience in pre-production as well as shipping titles.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Capacity Engineering
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

Anthropic manages one of the largest and fastest-growing infrastructure fleets in the industry — spanning multiple accelerator families, CPU families, and clouds. The Capacity Engineering team is responsible for making sure all of our infrastructure resources are accounted for, well-utilized, and efficiently allocated. We own the data, tooling, and operational systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization across first-party and third-party compute — one of the company's largest areas of spend.

As the Senior Engineering Manager for Capacity Engineering, you will lead the team that builds and operates these production systems. You'll set technical direction, grow and develop a team of senior and staff-level engineers, and be accountable for the reliability and correctness of surfaces that leadership, research engineering, inference, infrastructure, and finance all depend on. This is a hands-on leadership role: we expect you to stay close enough to the systems to review designs, make sound architectural calls, and step into an incident when the team needs you — while spending most of your time on people, priorities, and cross-organizational alignment.

The team's work spans three overlapping areas, and you'll be responsible for balancing investment across them as business priorities shift:

• Data platform — Pipelines that ingest occupancy and utilization telemetry from Kubernetes clusters, normalize billing and usage across cloud providers, and serve the BigQuery tables the rest of the org queries against. Consumers range from research engineers to finance to leadership, so this is product work as much as engineering.

• Planning and Assurance — Making the state of the fleet legible and actionable in real time: cluster health tooling, capacity planning platforms, alerting on occupancy drops and allocation problems, and systemic fixes to scheduling and fragmentation.

• Efficiency — Measuring and improving how effectively every major workload uses the hardware it runs on, across training, inference, and evals. Building benchmarking infrastructure and per-config baselines, then partnering with system-owning teams to close the gaps.

Key Responsibilities

• Be hands-on, lead and grow the team. Hire, onboard, coach, and retain senior and staff engineers. Set clear expectations, give direct and timely feedback, run performance and leveling conversations, and build a team culture that values ownership, rigor, and collaboration.

• Champion your internal customers. We build for our own use cases, so the teams that depend on our systems — research engineering, inference, infrastructure, and finance — are your customers. Engage with them directly, bring what you learn back into the roadmap, and lead the team in building tools people genuinely want to use.

• Own the roadmap. Translate company-level compute strategy into a prioritized engineering roadmap across data platform, planning and efficiency. Make explicit trade-offs when priorities compete, and communicate them clearly upward and outward.

• Set the technical bar. Review designs, weigh in on architecture, and hold the team to production standards — well-tested Python and SQL, latency and completeness SLOs, gap detection, and on-call that is sustainable.

• Run the team as a product organization. Ensure the team gathers its own requirements, defines schema contracts, and designs for a wide range of consumers — from research engineers to a CFO. Treat data quality and discoverability as first-class deliverables.

• Be the primary partner for cross-functional stakeholders. Work closely with infrastructure, inference, research engineering, and finance leadership to align on capacity decisions, efficiency targets, and spend. Represent the team's data and recommendations to senior leadership.

• Drive operational excellence. Own reliability and incident response for load-bearing systems, establish SLOs and on-call practices, and continuously reduce operational toil so the team can spend its time on higher-leverage work.

• Scale the function. As the fleet diversifies (every new provider is a net-new integration), anticipate where the team needs to grow in headcount, skills, and systems — and make the case for it.

What You Bring

• Experience managing software or infrastructure engineering teams, including hiring senior engineers, managing performance, and developing people into larger scope.

• A strong technical background in production systems — data engineering, infrastructure, distributed systems, or observability — with hands-on experience you can still draw on when reviewing designs or debugging with the team.

• Familiarity with at least one major cloud provider (AWS, GCP, or Azure), Kubernetes-based infrastructure, and modern observability stacks (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana).

• A track record of setting and executing an engineering roadmap in an ambiguous, high-autonomy environment with many stakeholders and shifting priorities.

• Excellent communication skills: you can explain a utilization metric to a research engineer and a spend forecast to a CFO, and you can advocate clearly for your team's priorities with senior leadership.

• Comfort owning operational responsibility for systems the company depends on, including on-call and incident management.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience leading teams working on capacity planning, resource management, product engineering or FinOps at a hyperscaler or in a large-scale ML environment.

• Familiarity with accelerator infrastructure — GPU metrics (DCGM), TPU utilization, or ML training and inference systems at the hardware level.

• Experience with multi-cloud billing and telemetry normalization (billing exports, reservation APIs, commitments, on-demand capacity reservations).

• Experience building or leading internal data products with self-service access, schema contracts, and documentation.

• Background in scheduling, packing efficiency, or profiling-driven optimization of large distributed workloads.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$405,000—$485,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Lead Scheduler (Data Center Due Diligence and Preconstruction)
jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend is seeking a Lead Scheduler to own the schedule review discipline for a confidential hyperscale data center client, both setting the standard other reviewers work to and carrying a portfolio of independent schedule reviews yourself. You will test whether developer-provided delivery dates are realistic, and you will decide what a rigorous review looks like for everyone doing that work alongside you.

This is a working lead role: part senior reviewer, part team lead. On your own deals, you review developer schedules from the ground up, test critical path and delivery dates, and flag plainly what the data does not support, the same work as everyone on your team. Beyond your own deals, you set the method: what a complete schedule review covers, what evidence standard it has to meet, and how findings get checked before they reach a client. You decide where the team's time goes based on risk and urgency, and you are the second set of eyes on the higher-stakes findings.

This is not a delivery role, and it does not replace the Program Manager's ownership of the overall risk picture on any deal. You and your team provide the schedule evidence; the Program Manager builds the risk picture from it and carries it to the client's deal team. It is also not a purely managerial role: you keep a real caseload of your own, current on the same tools and standards you are asking your team to meet.

This role works closely with Program Managers across your region and with the leads of the other review disciplines. The preferred locations are San Francisco or Northern Virginia. Remote can be considered for the right candidate.

Responsibilities

• Schedule review: Assess developer construction schedules from the ground up: logic, critical path and near-critical activity credibility, float, and sequencing. Confirm whether the delivery date, power connection, and commissioning and testing timelines are actually realistic, against the client's and our team's benchmarks.
• Supply chain and resourcing: Review the equipment and staffing plan behind a schedule, including long lead equipment orders and resource loading, and confirm whether the labor and materials backing the dates are firm commitments or assumptions.
• Evidence discipline: Be precise about what is known versus what is assumed. State plainly whether a number or date is confirmed, estimated, or simply what the developer has claimed, and hold your team to the same standard.
• Risk identification: Flag the risks a clean-looking schedule hides: long lead equipment, permitting, utility connections, seasonal weather, and compressed commissioning windows.
• Trend and variance analysis: Track how each schedule moves from one review to the next, not just a single point-in-time snapshot, and flag material variances and their likely cause.
• Acceleration analysis: Where a date is at risk, assess what could actually recover time, and which options are real versus cosmetic.
• Delivery handover: At construction start, make sure a clear schedule record, what was confirmed, what was assumed, and what is still an open risk, is handed to the onsite construction team on every deal your team touches.
• Setting the standard: Define what a complete, defensible schedule review looks like: the checklist, the depth of testing, and the level of evidence required, and hold every review on the team to it.
• Team allocation: Decide where the team's time goes across a shifting set of deals, based on where the risk and urgency are highest, and resolve it when demand outpaces capacity.
• Quality control: Review your team's higher-stakes findings before they reach a client, catching gaps or unsupported claims before anyone else does.
• Benchmarking: Build and maintain the library of schedule benchmarks, typical durations for long lead equipment, permitting, energization, and commissioning, that the whole team reviews against, so judgment calls are grounded in real data rather than memory.
• Training and development: Bring new reviewers up to the team's standard, and develop the judgment of less experienced schedule reviewers over time.
• Process improvement: Build and refine the templates, tools, and checklists the schedule discipline runs on as the portfolio and the team grow.

SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

• 10 - 15 years of planning and scheduling experience, data center or other mission-critical facility delivery strongly preferred.
• Preferably located in/near San Francisco, CA or Northern VA but will consider remote candidates as well as long as they are able to travel occasionally for site visits and team collaboration.
• Demonstrated ability to independently review and challenge someone else's development and construction schedule, not just build one.
• Prior experience training, mentoring, or reviewing the work of other schedule or planning professionals.
• Working fluency in P6 or equivalent scheduling software, including logic, critical path, and float credibility.
• Familiarity with earned value management (EVM) or similar progress-measurement methods, to independently sanity-check a developer's reported percent complete against actual schedule progress.
• Practical knowledge of long lead equipment timelines, utility and energization sequencing, permitting, and commissioning and testing durations in complex facility construction.
• Understanding of acceleration levers in data center construction, and the judgment to tell a real one from a cosmetic one.
• Comfortable delivering a difficult finding to a developer directly, professionally, and on a deadline, and comfortable holding a colleague's work to that same standard.
• Able to work from incomplete or dated information and state the caveats plainly, rather than waiting for a perfect dataset.
• Proven ability to manage competing priorities across multiple concurrent projects, and across a team's workload, not just your own.
• Strong written communication. Findings need to be usable by people who were not in the review, and feed directly into the client-facing due diligence report.
• AACE PSP or PMI-SP certification is a plus, not required.
• Technologically proficient, including MS Suite and Google Workspace in addition to scheduling software.

Project/Program Specifications

• Market sector experience: Data center development, mission critical facilities, or complex technical and hyperscale buildings strongly preferred.
• Program specific responsibilities: Independent schedule review across a portfolio of concurrent pre-lease diligence deals, plus ownership of the review method, benchmarks, and quality standard for the wider schedule review team.
• Software specific requirements: P6 or equivalent scheduling software, MS Suite, and Google Workspace.
• Travel: Minimal, approximately 3 days per month, plus occasional site visits and team collaboration.

The salary range for this role is $170,000 - $210,000. This range reflects the company's good faith estimate of the base salary for this position at the time of the posting. Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity. In addition to base salary, employees may be eligible for bonuses and a comprehensive benefits package.

*On-site presence and requirements may change depending on our client's needs.

Our inspired people share our vision and mission. We provide a great place to work, where each person has the opportunity and voice to affect change.

We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance.

jobs.title: Senior Research Associate, Molecular Biology and Sequencing
jobs.description:
What if… you could pioneer a new approach to designing life’s most essential molecules?

FL116, backed by Flagship Pioneering, is an early-stage biotechnology company transforming the way biomolecules are synthesized. Our innovative platform has the potential to transform how critical research, diagnostic, and therapeutic molecules are manufactured. We are seeking passionate problem solvers ready to make a profound impact on biotechnology and therapeutic innovation.

Position Summary

Senior Research Associate – Molecular Biology & Sequencing

We are seeking a motivated, detail-oriented, and technically strong Sr. RA to join our Assay Development team. This role owns the next-generation sequencing and high-throughput cloning that generate the design-build-test-learn data powering our platform —

You will run Illumina MiSeq i100 and NextSeq 2000 instruments end to end, build and QC large pooled variant libraries, and partner closely with enzyme engineering, chemical biology, and computational colleagues to turn sequencing output into actionable insight.

This is an exciting opportunity to build and own core molecular biology capabilities within a fast-paced, collaborative startup. You are a hands-on experimentalist who thrives on rigorous execution, cares about data quality and sample provenance, and is eager to grow with a rapidly evolving technology platform.

Key Responsibilities

• Sequencing: Perform NGS library preparation, QC, and end-to-end operation of Illumina MiSeq i100 and NextSeq 2000 platforms, including run setup and troubleshooting

• Cloning: Execute high-throughput molecular cloning workflows (Gibson, Golden Gate, and related methods) to build constructs and variant libraries at scale

• Pooled library assembly and QC: Assemble, quantify, and quality-control large pooled variant libraries, ensuring coverage, diversity, and representation meet project requirements

• Sample management and tracking: Own sample management, barcoding, and data/metadata tracking across both sequencing and cloning workflows, maintaining accurate records in ELN/LIMS systems

• Develop, optimize, and document robust, scalable protocols; identify and implement opportunities for throughput, cost, and quality improvements

• Process and interpret raw sequencer output, working with computational colleagues to convert reads into actionable insights for platform and pipeline decisions

• Collaborate closely with cross-functional partners across enzyme science, chemical biology, and machine learning to ensure sequencing and cloning capabilities meet downstream needs

• Maintain rigorous experimental documentation, communicate results clearly, and contribute to knowledge sharing and lab best practices

• Comply with laboratory safety protocols and best practices in reagent, sample, and biohazard handling

Qualifications

• B.S. in Biology, Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, or a related discipline with 5+ years of relevant laboratory experience; M.S. with 3+ years.

• Extensive hands-on experience performing NGS library preparation, library QC, and sequencer operation on Illumina MiSeq and NextSeq platforms

• Hands-on experience performing Gibson, Golden Gate, and related molecular cloning workflows

• Demonstrated ability to generate high-quality, reproducible data with rigorous documentation and sample tracking

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple parallel workstreams

• Clear communicator who works effectively in fast-paced, collaborative laboratory environments

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience characterizing the products of nucleic acid modifying enzymes via sequencing and other analytical methods (LC-MS, HPLC, etc.)

• Experience converting raw sequencer output into actionable insights, including familiarity with demultiplexing, read QC, and basic analysis tooling (e.g., command line, Python, or R)

• Experience applying high-throughput cloning and NGS data to enzyme engineering projects

• Experience running high-throughput enzyme assays using basic lab automation (e.g., liquid handlers) and plate readers

• Experience constructing and testing large variant libraries through pooled functional testing (e.g., yeast surface display or a related method)

• Familiarity with electronic lab notebooks (ELNs), LIMS, or related data-management tools

Who You Are

• Innovative Pioneer: You are excited by the opportunity to explore new scientific frontiers and to build the molecular biology capabilities that unlock a novel synthesis platform.

• Collaborative Contributor: You work effectively across teams, communicate clearly, and value shared success in a highly interdisciplinary environment.

• Inventive Problem Solver: You approach challenges with curiosity and creativity, troubleshooting from first principles to develop elegant, reliable experimental solutions.

• Rigorous Operator: You take pride in clean data, careful sample provenance, and protocols others can trust and reproduce.

• Mission-Driven Individual: You are motivated by the opportunity to fundamentally change how biomolecules are synthesized and to impact human health and biotechnology.

More About Flagship Pioneering

Flagship Pioneering conceives, creates, resources, and develops first-in-category life sciences companies to transform human health and sustainability. Since its launch in 2000, Flagship has originated and fostered more than 100 scientific ventures, generating billions in value. Flagship companies are known for addressing humanity’s most pressing challenges and advancing innovative solutions with global impact.

We are an equal opportunity employer and are dedicated to building diverse and inclusive teams. If you have some of the qualifications listed above but not all, we still encourage you to apply. We value passion, experience in many forms, and unique backgrounds.

Come pioneer the future with us.
